• Ability to communicate technical issues and solutions across all levels of the organization

At August Health, our mission is to empower the essential work of caring for our elders.
We achieve this by providing a modern operating platform and electronic health record (EHR) that enables senior living operators to deliver high-quality care with confidence.
Caregivers are the heart of senior living communities, embodying care, compassion, and well-being. Yet, they face increasing challenges—higher resident acuity, complex workflows, and staffing shortages. At August Health, we build tools that simplify their tasks, eliminate inefficiencies, and provide the insights they need to focus on what truly matters—caring for residents.
At August, we strive to live our values each day, in every interaction with our customers and with each other.
• Be responsible – leave things better than you found them
• Take ownership – be decisive and take action
• Be ambitious – build something great

• Track requests, document configuration decisions, and communicate progress clearly using internal ticketing and project management tools.
• Collaborate with Customer Experience, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams to troubleshoot complex issues, identify recurring patterns, and improve how we deliver configuration services.
• Help develop and improve internal processes, documentation, and tools that make configuration work more accurate, efficient, and scalable.
## Who You Are
• 2–4 years of experience in a systems analyst, business analyst, implementation, technical operations, or similar role involving hands-on software configuration and data management.
• Experience working with complex software platforms where system settings, workflows, and data structures interact to drive end-user behavior.
• Experience working within ticketing or project management systems such as Linear, Intercom, Jira, or Zendesk.

We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.
When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.
Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.
We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. The Business Operations team sits within Finance and partners across Chainalysis to strengthen how the company plans, makes decisions, and executes. Combining analytical rigor with practical operating judgment, the team helps leaders translate company priorities into clear plans, effective operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. As Chainalysis continues to evolve, Business Operations also helps build the processes and ways of working that enable teams to scale and adapt.
You’ll join a close-knit, highly cross-functional team working with partners across Finance, R&D, go-to-market, Legal, Security, and beyond. The team takes on high-priority work across the business, often creating structure where approaches are still taking shape, and helps teams align and move change forward. This role offers broad exposure to Chainalysis and the opportunity to help shape how the company operates through its next stage of growth.
In this role, you’ll:
As a Senior Business Operations Analyst at Chainalysis, you will be a strategic operator and connective tissue across leadership and functions - helping translate company priorities into clear plans, operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes. You’ll partner with leaders across Finance, Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and other teams to improve how the business plans, makes decisions, and executes.
You’ll support high-priority, cross-functional initiatives end to end: framing ambiguous problems, developing analyses and recommendations, aligning stakeholders, establishing milestones and governance, and driving follow-through. You’ll help run planning and business review cadences, build KPI reporting and insights, improve processes and systems, and support change initiatives such as pricing and packaging, go-to-market readiness, product launches, and organizational or operating-model changes.
We are looking for candidates with:
• 5+ years of proven experience in business operations, strategy and operations, ideally in a fast-paced technology environment.
• Strong project and program management skills, including prioritization, stakeholder management, and attention to detail.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into insights, recommendations, and decisions.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create executive-ready narratives and materials.
• Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation and measurable outcomes.
• Supporting annual or quarterly planning, operating cadences, business reviews, resource allocation, or strategic planning processes.
• Establishing KPIs, building performance dashboards, and using data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
• Ability to drive clarity in ambiguity, influence without authority, and demonstrate resilience in a dynamic environment.
• Curious, adaptable, and motivated to learn quickly, challenge assumptions, and make the company and team better.
Nice to have experience:
• Supporting pricing and packaging, go-to-market or commercialization initiatives, product launches, or broader change-management efforts.
• Management consulting, finance, program management in Tech, FinTech, Blockchain other similar.
• Familiarity with business intelligence, data, and collaboration tools; experience with Jira, Confluence, Databricks, spreadsheets, SQL, and/or AI-powered tools.
AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.
AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.
About Chainalysis
Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.
You belong here.
At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

Turn data into decisions

• Build dashboards and forecasts that show performance across the self-serve customer journey and explain changes to business stakeholders.
• Evaluate experiments, automated journeys, and agentic programs using measures such as reach, completion, escalation, conversion, retained ARR, and expansion ARR.
• Surface qualified digital intent signals for sales teams and measure the outcomes of sales-assisted handoffs especially related to upsell motion.

• Strong SQL skills and experience analyzing customer-level data in a cloud data platform such as Databricks.
• Experience with digital funnels, product event data, cohorts, dashboards, and experiment measurement.
• Working knowledge of SaaS measures including ARR, GRR, NRR, churn, expansion, customer acquisition cost, and lifetime value.
• Ability to explain findings in clear business terms.
## Helpful Experience
• Pendo or a similar product analytics platform; Zuora, Salesforce, web analytics, and a BI tool.
• Churn or expansion propensity analysis, pricing measurement, or evaluation of automated customer journeys.

Junction is building the infrastructure layer for diagnostic healthcare, making patient data accessible, actionable, and automated across labs and devices. Our mission is simple but ambitious: build the infrastructure that makes predictive, personalized care possible.
If you're passionate about how technology can supercharge healthcare, you’ll fit right in.
Backed by Creandum, Point Nine, 20VC, YC , and leading angels, we’re working to solve one of the biggest challenges of our time: making healthcare personalized, proactive, and affordable. We’re already connecting millions and scaling fast.
## Short on time? TL;DR:
• You: An integration or implementation specialist who can write and ship your own code. You’ve worked closely with partners and technology to move things along, you reach for tools like Claude or Codex to build your own solutions, and you’d rather automate a process than repeat it.
• Us: A team of ~60 connecting digital health companies to labs like Quest and LabCorp.
## Why we need you
Getting a new customer live with one of our lab partners means proving that their data is landing in our system exactly right. We’re doing that for about 30 accounts at once, with no sign of it slowing down. Nobody owns this fully today. You'll be the first person to take it end-to-end and build the automation that makes it basically run itself.
Certification is the first problem we need you to solve, but it’s not the last: across 20+ lab partners, there’s a similar list of manual processes waiting for the same treatment, and they’re yours to turn into real integrations and automations.
You’ll have genuine license to build, with AI as your main lever, working alongside Oliver and Andy , and closely with Jeff . For the right person, it’s a strong first step into solutions engineering.
## What you'll be doing day to day
• Own lab certifications end-to-end: pick up new requests from Quest and LabCorp, build the test plan, run the cases, and get each account over the line.
• Keep ~30 moving at once: know where every certification stands and chase whatever is stuck without being asked.
• Be the go-to person for our lab partners: reliable, organized back-and-forth with Quest, LabCorp, and our other partners on test cases and issues.
• Push the automation further: a lot of certification work today is still manual, and we expect most of the happy path to be automated within the next year. You’ll be the one building that — with scripts, agents, whatever cuts the manual work — not just running the process by hand.
• Get hands-on with the data: dig into our backend, databases, and API responses when a result doesn’t land the way it should — in practice this means running scripts yourself (sandbox overrides, Quest order pulls, HL7 changes), not flagging it for someone else to fix.
• Run the other partner processes: set up lab accounts and sub-accounts, track pricing requests, and make sure our team always knows where things stand.
• Keep customers informed: maintain the docs that explain certification and account setup to customers and our sales team.
• Find the next process to fix: spot other lab workflows that are manual and repetitive, and make the case for automating them.
## What success looks like
• Every certification and partner process has a clear owner, status, and next step. Nobody has to ask where things stand.
• Accounts go live faster, with less back-and-forth with our partners.
• At least one more lab partner process has moved out of a spreadsheet or inbox and into something that mostly runs itself.
## What we're looking for
• Implementation or integrations experience: 2+ years running implementations, integrations, or technical support for an API-based or similarly technical product.
• Ecosystem thinking: you've worked somewhere with an active network of partners and integrations, not just a customer and a vendor. You understand that improving a process with a lab partner affects our customer and our customer's customer.
• Technically minded: you can make code changes and ship fixes yourself — in a script, a database query, or an API integration — without needing an engineer to review your work line by line. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need real coding ability, not just comfort reading code.
• Hands-on scripting: you’re comfortable writing SQL and scripting in Python or JavaScript — this is how you’ll actually get the job done.
• AI-native: you already use AI tools every day and have built them into your workflows. When something is repetitive, AI is the first thing you reach for.
• Project management: you can keep dozens of things moving at once without anything slipping.
• High ownership: you see a problem and want to solve it next. The best person for this role looks at the manual work and decides it shouldn't need a human.
• Dependable with partners: you're clear, organized, and responsive with outside contacts, and you'll represent Junction with our lab partners.
• Nice to have: experience with lab or healthcare data (HL7, results interfaces, EMRs), SQL, or scripting in Python or JavaScript.
You don't need to tick every box to fit in here. If the problems we're solving genuinely interest you and you know you can contribute, we'd love to talk.
## What this role isn't
• You're looking for a customer success role: you'll talk to customers when it helps get them live, but most of your time is with lab partners and our internal teams.
• You want a pure engineering role: you'll work with code and data, but the job is owning a process and automating it, not shipping product. With that said, this isn’t a role where you can avoid code — you’ll be writing and shipping changes yourself, just not building product features.

## About your role
We're redesigning Juniper Square's Lead-to-Cash process end to end, from the first marketing touch through billing and recognized revenue. We're hiring a Lead Business Systems Analyst to own the business design behind it: the commercial model (product catalog, legal entity, currency, billing determinants, and lifecycle) and the process and data requirements at every point where a deal moves from one system to the next. This is a hands-on role: beyond defining requirements, you'll configure and build simple-to-medium-complexity changes in Salesforce and the CPQ yourself.
You'll work across a stack that includes Marketo, Salesforce, and Gong for go-to-market, a new CPQ platform, Ironclad for contracting, Zone Billing and NetSuite for billing and revenue, and Workato as the integration layer. This role will partner with our Lead-to-Cash program manager who owns sequencing, and you own the model and the requirements. If you've modeled complex fee structures down to the determinant level and want to design the right model rather than patch an inherited one, this will be a great role for you.
## What you’ll do
End-to-end process design
• Document the Lead-to-Cash process for new-logo and fund administration expansion deals, stage by stage, from demand capture to revenue recognition
• Define the target process, the system of record for each stage, and the hand-off rules between stages
Lead, account & opportunity model
• Define requirements for lead-to-account matching, routing to existing account owners, and opportunity creation in Salesforce
• Design how expansion opportunities are created and forecast, including by Fund Administration account managers
• Define how a deal is represented from quote through order, provisioning, invoice, and revenue, including the customer hierarchy (account, platform workspace, fund, entity)
Commercial model & CPQ
• Design an attribute-based product catalog and pricing model for software and fund administration services
• Define billing determinants for asset-based, entity-based, and activity-based fees, including where each value is sourced and how it is validated
• Define lifecycle events (start, amendment, escalation, suspension, termination) and decide which should be automated
• Write the requirements and acceptance criteria the CPQ implementation is built and tested against
Build & configure
• Configure and build simple-to-medium-complexity changes yourself in Salesforce and the CPQ: objects and fields, Flows, validation rules, page layouts, permission sets, reports and dashboards, and CPQ products, price rules, product rules, and approval rules
• Prototype solutions in a sandbox to validate requirements with stakeholders before they're finalized
• Hand off more complex work, such as Apex, integrations, and large data migrations, to our engineers with clear technical designs, and review what they build
• Ship your changes through our release process, with sandbox testing, peer review, version control, and documentation, so every change to financial and customer data stays auditable
Contract to cash
• Define the data exchange between the CPQ and Ironclad, so signed terms, including uplifts, become the contract of record
• Specify booking, onboarding, and billing triggers, and the subscription hand-off into Zone Billing and NetSuite, working with our Integrations Engineers
• Partner with Revenue Accounting so every design supports ASC 606 and SOX control requirements
Data, testing & governance
• Work with our Analytics Engineers so ARR and other key metrics can be computed from system data
• Design and lead UAT, and own the data mapping for migrating live subscriptions
• Own the commercial model's documentation and change process after go-live
What success looks like
• First 90 days: a documented end-to-end process for both motions, and a first draft of the target commercial model and customer hierarchy, reviewed with Sales, Finance, and Fund Administration leaders; your first Salesforce configuration changes shipped to production
• Within 6 months: an approved catalog, entity model, and acceptance criteria that the CPQ and integration builds are running against
• Within 12 months: every live subscription represented in the new model at the entity level, with billing determinants and signed terms flowing between systems without re-keying
## Qualifications
Required Qualifications

• Requirements experience across several Lead-to-Cash stages: lead management and routing, opportunity and forecasting, CPQ, contract management, billing, and revenue
• Have modeled asset-based, usage-based, or other non-seat fee structures down to the billing determinant level
• Deep experience designing product catalogs and pricing models in a CPQ (Salesforce CPQ or Revenue Cloud, Neu, DealHub, Conga, Zuora, or similar)
• Strong working knowledge of Salesforce and Zone Billing / NetSuite data models: leads, accounts, opp

## What is Loancrate?
We started Loancrate to make home-buying simpler and less expensive for lenders and borrowers. Today, mortgage lenders are stuck running their companies on software products built 20 years ago. These products are slow, unstable, and don't lead to material improvements in efficiency. When using these systems, the average human cost to originate a loan is still over $11,000.
Loancrate builds AI-native tooling to automate mortgage workflows. Our ultimate goal is fully automated origination, which has the potential to save lenders over $16B in operating expense per year.
Since starting in 2020, our remote team has enabled our customers to power >$85 billion in new home loans. We care about collaboration, very open communication covering the good & the bad so that we learn from our decisions quickly, and ultimately having fun while we're building. You'll fit in well if you like diving deep quickly!
## The Opportunity
Mortgage lenders don't switch loan origination systems lightly. An LOS transition touches every workflow a lender has - origination, processing, underwriting, closing - and it has to happen without slowing down the pipeline or losing a single file in the shuffle. We're looking for an Implementation Lead to own that transition from the project-management side: building the rollout plan, keeping every team on track to hit it, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks between sales, our Implementation Consultants, our Customer Success Managers, and the customer.
You'll own the full project plan for each customer implementation - milestones, timelines, who's doing what by when - while our CSMs and Implementation Consultants own the mortgage-advisory and hands-on configuration work with the customer. Your job is to be the person who can look at any implementation on any given day and say exactly where it stands, what's blocking it, and what has to happen next to hit go-live.
Because you’ll be running implementations for a mortgage lending product, you need firsthand experience leading a lender through an LOS transition. You’ve owned the project plan, coordinated the teams and dependencies, and helped take a lender through go-live. We can teach you Loancrate, our tooling, and our approach, but we’re looking for someone who already understands what it takes to keep an LOS transition moving.
This is a foundational role: you'll build the rollout methodology every future implementation follows, set the bar for how tightly we run project management across Customer Success, and be the person who turns "yes, Loancrate can do this" into a lender that's actually live.
## What You'll Do
• Own all project management for customer implementations - you're the single point of accountability for the plan, the timeline, and whether an implementation is on track.
• Define rollout milestones and keep every team organized around them - sales handoff, configuration, data migration, UAT, training, go-live - and make sure the Implementation Consultants, CSMs, and the customer's own team are aligned on what's due when.
• Keep Jira and Linear in sync and own regular project updates - maintain accurate statuses, owners, and next steps so customers and internal teams have a clear view of progress without having to chase for information.
• Own the coordination and follow-through for implementation meetings - prepare and distribute agendas, facilitate status discussions, capture decisions and action items, and follow up with owners so next steps keep moving.
• Build a repeatable rollout plan - turn what you learn from each implementation into a playbook and template the next one can start from, instead of rebuilding the plan from scratch every time.
• Flag risks and dependencies early - identify when a milestone is at risk, bring the right people together to resolve blockers, and escalate decisions with clear context and timeline impacts.
• Partner closely with CSMs and Implementation Consultants - you own the plan, they own the mortgage-advisory and configuration conversations with the customer; your job is to keep their work sequenced and on schedule.
• Be the internal voice for process - as we run more implementations in parallel, help Product and Engineering understand where timelines are getting stretched by product gaps versus process gaps.
• Willingness to travel - expect approximately once-a-month domestic US travel to customer sites, with occasional additional trips around key milestones like kickoff and go-live.
## What Success Looks Like
Within your first 90 days, you will:
• Be running the project plan for at least one active customer implementation, with milestones defined and Jira/Linear set up to keep the customer automatically informed.
• Have a clear, repeatable rollout plan template that the next implementation can be built from.
• Have run implementation meetings end-to-end - agenda, discussion, and clear next steps - without needing someone else to drive them.
• Have a direct working relationship with the Implementation Consultants and CSMs on your implementations, with a clear, mutually understood division of who owns what.
By the 12-18 month mark, you'll have run multiple lender implementations end-to-end, refined the rollout methodology into something the next hire can pick up with minimal ramp, and be a candidate to help build and lead a broader Implementation/PMO function as we scale.

## What is Loancrate?
We started Loancrate to make home-buying simpler and less expensive for lenders and borrowers. Today, mortgage lenders are stuck running their companies on software products built 20 years ago. These products are slow, unstable, and don't lead to material improvements in efficiency. When using these systems, the average human cost to originate a loan is still over $11,000.
Loancrate builds AI-native tooling to automate mortgage workflows. Our ultimate goal is fully automated origination, which has the potential to save lenders over $16B in operating expense per year.
Since starting in 2020, our remote team has enabled our customers to power >$85 billion in new home loans. We care about collaboration, very open communication covering the good & the bad so that we learn from our decisions quickly, and ultimately having fun while we're building. You'll fit in well if you like diving deep quickly!
## The Opportunity
Buying a new loan origination system is the easy part. Actually configuring it to match how a lender runs its business - their conditions, their disclosures, their underwriting guidelines, their quirks - is where implementations are won or lost. We're looking for an Implementation Consultant to be the person in the room (virtually or on-site) who makes that configuration work actually happen.
This is a forward-deployed, hands-on role. You'll work directly with a lender's team during the implementation phase to configure Loancrate around their workflows, answer their configuration questions, and get them through user acceptance testing. Once the customer is live, you roll off and move to the next implementation - the CSM stays on as the long-term relationship owner, and the Implementation Lead keeps the overall project plan on track, while you're the one actually in the product with the customer making it work.
Because this role sits inside an active mortgage workflow from day one, you need to already be fluent in mortgage - not learning it as you go. We can teach you Loancrate inside and out. What we can't do in any reasonable timeframe is teach you what a lender's processors and underwriters actually need a system to do for them.
This is a foundational role on a team we're building from scratch: you'll help define what "good configuration" looks like, build the muscle memory for how we implement lenders quickly and correctly, and be one of the people whose work most directly determines whether a customer's go-live goes smoothly.
## What You'll Do
• Act as the forward-deployed implementation expert - work directly with the customer's team to configure Loancrate around their specific workflows, conditions, and business rules.
• Translate a lender's current-system setup into a Loancrate configuration - take how they operate today and recommend (and build) the configuration that gets them the same outcome, or better, in Loancrate.
• Own testing support during UAT - respond to configuration and testing questions as they come in, and work the "UAT Blocked" queue in Jira so customer-reported blockers get resolved quickly instead of sitting.
• Troubleshoot configuration issues in real time - when something isn't behaving the way the customer expects, you're the one who can dig in, find the root cause, and fix it or escalate it clearly.
• Work closely with the Implementation Lead and CSM - you're heads-down on configuration and testing; they're managing the timeline and the broader relationship, and you keep them informed of anything that could affect either.
• Roll off cleanly at go-live - document the final configuration and any open items clearly enough that the CSM can pick up the relationship without a gap.
• Help build the implementation playbook - common configuration patterns, frequently asked setup questions, and testing checklists that make the next implementation faster than the last.
• Willingness to travel - expect approximately once-a-month domestic US travel to customer sites, with occasional additional trips around key milestones like UAT kickoff and go-live.
## What Success Looks Like
Within your first 90 days, you will:
• Be the hands-on configuration owner on at least one active implementation, trusted by the customer to answer setup questions directly.
• Have cleared UAT-Blocked tickets at a pace that keeps testing moving rather than stalling on your queue.
• Have handled a real configuration curveball - a workflow that doesn't map cleanly to Loancrate - and worked it to a resolution the customer was happy with.
• Have a direct working relationship with your Implementation Lead and CSM, with a clear handoff process for when you roll off a project.
By the 12-18 month mark, you'll have implemented multiple lenders end-to-end, be a go-to resource for tricky configuration scenarios, and be a candidate to help train and ramp future Implementation Consultants as the team grows.
## Required Skills and Background
• Direct mortgage experience - you've worked at a lender or mortgage tech company and understand the origination-to-closing lifecycle (1003, LE, CD, AUS findings, conditions, lock extensions) well enough to configure a system around it without hand-holding.
• Hands-on experience with a loan origination system (Encompass, Empower, Byte, or similar) - you've worked inside one, ideally helped configure or administer one, and know where lenders' real-world workflows get tricky.
• Comfort working hands-on in software configuration - you're not afraid to get into settings, rules, and workflows yourself rather than just describing what needs to change to someone else.
• Testing and troubleshooting instincts - you can read a bug report or a UAT ticket, reproduce the issue, and tell the difference between a configuration fix, a training gap, and an actual product bug.

• Comfort with a project-phase role - you're energized by the intensity of an implementation and the clean handoff at the end, rather than wanting to own the long-term relationship.

Neural Concept embeds AI into design and simulation workflows so engineering teams make continuous, data-driven decisions instead of waiting on sequential design–simulation–validation cycles. None of that matters until the platform is running inside the customer's environment, on their infrastructure, under their rules.
That is this role. You take an enterprise customer and make the platform real for them: architected, deployed, integrated, cleared by their security organisation, and stable enough that their engineers stop thinking about it. You own that outcome end to end for named accounts, as their primary technical counterpart.
What you will do
• The deployment, from the first architecture conversation through go-live and into steady-state operation.
• Its integration with the customer's identity, data and engineering systems, and the infrastructure and model serving layer beneath it.
• The relationship with their IT, security and platform teams: assessments, architecture reviews, and the call when something breaks.
• The diagnosis when it does break, including when the cause sits outside our own software.
• The runbooks, post-mortems and playbooks that make the next deployment easier, and the feedback loop into Product.
Where you will do it
Managed Kubernetes across the major clouds. On-premises and fully air-gapped clusters with no route to the internet, GPU infrastructure, self-hosted model serving. Customer HPC environments, schedulers, and shared storage under real load.
If installing software with no internet access, on hardware you do not control, reads as the interesting part of the job rather than the obstacle, this will suit you.
Who you are
You will often be the only Neural Concept engineer in the room. We are looking for someone with:
• 6+ years deploying and operating enterprise software in production, two of them in environments you did not control.
• Kubernetes at configuration depth: how chart values become rendered manifests, and why a workload will not start.
• Identity and SSO fundamentals: OIDC and SAML, clients and credential rotation, redirect URIs, group-to-role mapping.
• Linux, networking and TLS: DNS, routing, ingress and egress, certificate chains and interception proxies.
• Kubernetes storage: persistent volumes and CSI, access modes, diagnosing shared storage that degrades under load.
• A production deployment you personally carried and then supported. Name it, date it, tell us what went wrong.
• Professional customer-facing English , and willingness to travel and work your customers' hours.
Also valuable: regulated or air-gapped deployments · private registries and image mirroring · GPU scheduling and LLM serving · enterprise IdP administration · Terraform and GitOps · Prometheus and Grafana · HPC schedulers · ISO 27001 evidence · Python · PLM, CAD or CAE exposure.
You Get
• Work with a world-class technology team – our engineers are top-notch, and we always aim for excellence.
• Benefit from a competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.
• Thrive in a collaborative, multicultural environment where your work is visible and recognized.
• Develop professionally alongside talented colleagues who share knowledge freely and support one another.
• Make a global impact by helping customers shift to AI-assisted design, making innovation faster, smarter, and more sustainable.
• Balance life and work with remote work or hybrid model (20% remote) —we care about results, not rigid schedules.
• Enjoy paid vacations, healthcare (medical/vision/dental), 401K matching
Where You Will Be
• San Mateo, California;
• Travelling: This position will require travelling to customer locations in the US.
• Start date: ASAP

Remote, worldwide · Freelance course project with a path to full-time
We’re hiring on behalf of a global hands-on tech-education platform used by over a million engineers to learn DevOps, cloud , Kubernetes and AI . Its courses are built around real labs, not slides, and taught by practising engineers who are great on camera.
We’re looking for a machine learning practitioner who loves teaching to create and present ML courses for engineers, from foundations to training their own models.
This role suits you if you already teach as part of what you do: you’ve published courses on Udemy, Pluralsight, Coursera or YouTube, written a book, taught at a university or bootcamp, or regularly run workshops and talks.
How it works
• It starts with one paid course project. You can do it alongside your current job. There’s no fixed weekly-hour requirement, just a delivery plan you agree on together. A typical project takes around 3 months.
• The goal is long-term. The team is growing its internal trainer pool, and the first project is how both sides find out if it’s a fit. After that, it can lead to a full-time role or more course projects.
• A fixed fee per course is agreed upfront, based on course length and topic complexity. Fees are competitive, and advanced topics and exceptional instructors are paid accordingly. Payment is made on delivery of the completed course.
• Fully remote with flexible hours. Expect a weekly sync, Slack communication, and some time-zone overlap with a Europe/Asia-based team.
What you’ll do
• Shape the course with the curriculum team: sections, lessons, labs and notebooks.
• Write lab specs that a dedicated labs team builds, then test them.
• Write and narrate short, story-driven video lessons (about 6 minutes each) that make ML intuitive. You’re welcome to use AI to draft, but the final script should sound like you.
• Record demo and lab-solution walkthroughs.
• Work through structured editorial feedback, especially on your first section.
Video editing, animation, lab infrastructure and publishing are all handled by the production team. You focus on the teaching.
What we’re looking for
• Strong, hands-on ML foundations: you’ve trained, evaluated and shipped models yourself (scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow).
• The ability to explain the “why” behind ML clearly to engineers new to it.
• Excellent spoken and written English. All courses are scripted, narrated and delivered in English, so you need clear, natural, easily understood English and confidence on camera.
• A genuine passion for teaching, shown through courses, tutorials, talks, workshops or mentoring you’ve done because you enjoy it.
• Current with the field and keen to keep learning.
• Clear, engaging spoken English and confidence on camera.
• Openness to an established teaching methodology and to editorial feedback.
Nice to have
• Published online courses, a book, or university/bootcamp teaching experience.
• Experience with fine-tuning, MLOps or deploying models in production.
• Cloud ML certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP, Databricks ).
How to apply
Send your CV or LinkedIn profile, plus a link that shows how you teach: a course, a talk, a tutorial or a short video.

## About Opal Security:
At Opal, we’re building modern identity governance for the AI era—intelligent access management that empowers enterprises to move fast while staying secure. Our mission is to bring clarity, control, and confidence to complex enterprise environments, helping teams govern access without slowing down innovation.
## About the Role
When a customer's access workflow breaks at 9am on a Monday, or a new enterprise team needs to be live by the end of the quarter, they should be able to count on one engineer who knows Opal inside out.
We're hiring a Senior Customer Success Engineer to be that person. You'll be the technical owner of our customers' experience after the sale: you'll get them implemented and integrated, troubleshoot the hard problems, and teach their teams to run Opal confidently. You'll work hand in hand with our Strategic CSM, who owns the executive relationships, so you can stay close to the product and the code.
## Your responsibilities
• Be the technical support lead for enterprise customers. Take tier 2/3 issues from tickets and shared Slack channels, investigate bugs and misconfigurations first, and bring engineering a clear reproduction when it needs to go further. Stay accountable until it's resolved. Work to defined response targets by severity.
• Drive technical adoption. Help customers roll Opal out to more teams, apps and resources, run enablement sessions and office hours, and watch for configuration and usage patterns that signal a problem or an opening. Pass what you find to the Strategic CSM.
• Lead customer implementations. Run technical kickoff, design the integration plan, and take customers from first connection to go-live: identity provider and SSO setup, SCIM provisioning, cloud and app integrations, and Terraform or API-based configuration.
• Write what customers need. Contribute to public documentation, sample code, runbooks and troubleshooting guides, and turn recurring issues into articles or product fixes.
• Build the support and implementation playbook. Define severity levels, escalation paths, handoffs to engineering, and an implementation checklist. Choose and set up the tooling. Automate the repetitive work.
• Close the loop with product and engineering. Log and prioritize bugs, bring structured customer feedback to the people building Opal, and test fixes with customers.
## You Might Be a Fit If You:
• Have 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role. Technical support engineer, solutions engineer, technical account manager, implementation or professional services consultant, or customer success engineer, ideally in security or identity SaaS.
• Know identity and access. You understand SSO, SAML, OIDC and OAuth, SCIM provisioning, identity providers such as Okta or Entra ID, and how enterprises manage access and reviews. This is the most important technical area for the role.
• Know cloud and infrastructure as code. Hands-on with AWS, Azure or GCP, and with Terraform and Kubernetes.
• Have run implementations. You have taken customers from kickoff to go-live, scoped the work, and managed the risks and the customer's own team along the way.
• Communicate clearly. You write clear tickets, docs and customer updates, and stay calm and precise when a customer is frustrated.
• Like building the system. You have worked with a ticketing or support platform such as Zendesk, Linear or Jira, and you want to design severity levels, runbooks and playbooks, not only follow them.
• Thrive on being early. You've worked at a Series A-C company and built process while everything around you moved. You create clarity instead of waiting for it.
• Its OKAY if you haven’t worked early stage but you gotta want it!

Paradigm Health is rebuilding the clinical research ecosystem by enabling equitable access to trials for all patients. Our platform enhances trial efficiency and reduces the barriers to participation for healthcare providers. Incubated by ARCH Venture Partners and backed by leading healthcare and life sciences investors, Paradigm’s seamless infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations, will bring potentially life-saving therapies to patients faster.
Our team hails from a broad range of disciplines and is committed to the company’s mission to create equitable access to clinical trials for any patient, anywhere. Join us, and bring your expertise, passion, creativity, and drive as we work together to realize this mission.
About the role:
This is a hybrid role that blends the responsiveness of Tier 1 support with the technical depth of Tier 2. You will build and leverage purpose-built dashboards, investigation tooling, and AI-assisted agents to resolve the majority of tickets autonomously — reducing Engineering and Product dependency — while also serving as the internal expert who diagnoses root causes and drives continuous improvement in how support operates.
What you’ll do:
Triage & First-Response
• Serve as the primary contact for inbound support tickets from research sites, sponsor teams, and Clinical Operations staff via Zendesk
• Categorize, prioritize, and resolve common break-fix issues — login/access, account provisioning, platform navigation, standard trial workflow questions — within defined SLAs
• Monitor standard trial SLA milestones (patient surfacing timelines, appointment data receipt) using support dashboards; proactively flag anomalies before sites escalate
• Provide timely, clear, and professional responses to clinical coordinators, PIs, and sponsor program managers — often non-technical users — with appropriate context and next steps
Complex Investigation & Root Cause Analysis
• Investigate data discrepancies across the full pipeline: EHR/interface ingestion, department data filters, patient matching logic, and app-layer presentation — determining whether issues are isolated, site-specific, or systemic
• Diagnose interface-related issues (SIU feeds, HL7/FHIR file delivery, ingest delays) by reviewing interface go-live timelines, delivery logs, and ingestion history
• Triage patient-trial identification feedback — a high-frequency, high-complexity scenario — by examining data across interfaces, pipelines, and the application, and routing findings to the appropriate team (data discrepancy, trial configuration, pipeline bug, or app bug)
• Perform root cause analysis and produce clear summaries for both external users (sites and sponsors) and internal stakeholders (Engineering, Product, Technical Services)
Tooling, Automation & Continuous Improvement
• Build and maintain internal support tooling: investigation dashboards, triage applications, and AI-assisted agents that enable faster, more autonomous ticket resolution
• Implement and optimize Zendesk configurations to surface actionable metrics — resolution time, ticket priority, and ticket leakage (tickets that escalate beyond Support) — and drive continuous improvement
• Identify recurring issue patterns and build automated detection and response workflows where appropriate
• Maintain and expand the internal knowledge base: runbooks, issue playbooks, escalation criteria, and resolution documentation
• Participate in UAT and product release cycles to anticipate new support scenarios and update tooling proactively
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Serve as the liaison between the Support function and Engineering, Product, Informatics, and Technical Services — translating ticket patterns into structured defect reports and product feedback
• Maintain accurate ticket records; apply consistent tagging, priority, and resolution codes to enable downstream analytics and trend identification
• Track and report on core support KPIs: first-contact resolution rate, mean resolution time, escalation-to-engineering ratio, and ticket leakage rate
Who you are:
Required
• Bachelor's degree in health informatics, life sciences, computer science, clinical research, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience
• 6-9 years in a technical support, data operations, or client-facing technical role; health tech or regulated SaaS environment strongly preferred
• Working knowledge of clinical research operations: IRB, CRF, EDC, site coordinator workflows, patient recruitment lifecycle
• Hands-on SQL experience — ability to query databases to trace data flow, validate pipeline outputs, and identify missing or anomalous records
• Familiarity with data integration concepts: HL7 (SIU, ADT), FHIR, file-based ETL, interface monitoring
• HIPAA compliance knowledge and experience handling PHI in a technology context
• Proficiency with Zendesk or equivalent support platforms; comfort with configuration and reporting
• Strong analytical and written communication skills — able to produce rigorous root cause summaries for both technical and non-technical audiences
Preferred
• Experience building internal tooling, dashboards, or lightweight investigation apps (Python, no-code/low-code, or similar)
• Exposure to AI/LLM-assisted support tooling, triage agents, or workflow automation
• Familiarity with EHR systems (Epic, Cerner) and how clinical data is structured and delivered
• Experience with clinical trial platforms: CTMS, EDC (Medidata, Veeva), IRT, or eConsent systems
• Understanding of 21 CFR Part 11 (electronic records in regulated clinical environments)
• CCRP, CCRA, CPHIMS, or equivalent clinical/health informatics certification

## About the Role
We’re building our quality practice from the ground up, and you’ll be our first dedicated QA team member. Today, testing is handled by our developers and product team. Our mobile app is built in React Native and ships on both iOS and Android. You’ll start with hands-on manual testing across both platforms, then build the foundations for automation: UI/UX regression tests and software test fixtures that simulate point-of-sale (POS) terminals, so we’re no longer tied to physical hardware for every test cycle. Much of that work will be done in TypeScript and Node.js, so this role is a good fit for someone who enjoys writing code, debugging, and building tools. Because there’s no established QA team yet, you’ll work closely with the engineering team and have real influence shaping how we test, what tools we use, and how quality is measured.
This is a great fit for a curious, self-motivated person who wants to learn fast, take ownership early, and help define what QA looks like at our company.
## What You’ll Do
• Create our first formal end-to-end manual test plans and execute them on iOS and Android for new features, bug fixes, and release candidates
• Write clear, reusable test cases from product requirements, designs, and user stories, and organize them into a living test library
• Identify, document, and track defects with precise reproduction steps, noting whether issues are platform-specific or shared across iOS and Android, and work directly with developers to verify fixes
• Use Node.js and TypeScript tooling to debug issues, inspect logs and API traffic, and help pinpoint root causes
• Perform exploratory testing to uncover edge cases, device and OS-version differences, and usability issues
• Help establish baseline QA processes: bug reporting standards, release checklists, and test documentation
• Begin building automated UI/UX regression tests for our React Native app
• Develop test fixtures and mock services in TypeScript and Node.js that simulate POS terminal behavior, reducing our reliance on physical hardware
• Help evaluate and recommend testing tools and frameworks, and bring automated tests into our CI/CD pipeline over time
• Partner with engineers and product managers during project planning, standups, and release readiness reviews
## What We’re Looking For
## Required
• Hands-on programming experience in TypeScript/JavaScript and Node.js . You’re comfortable writing scripts and small services, working with async code, using npm, and debugging with logs. Coursework, internships, bootcamps, and personal projects all count.
• Working familiarity with React and React Native (components, props, state, hooks, and how a UI renders), enough to understand how our app behaves and where bugs tend to come from. Building even a small React Native project, such as a personal or course app, is great preparation.
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
• Understanding of the software development lifecycle and core QA concepts (test plans, test cases, regression and smoke testing, bug lifecycle)
• Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to problem-solving
• Self-motivation and comfort with ambiguity: you’ll often figure out the “how” yourself rather than follow an existing playbook
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the confidence to raise quality concerns with the engineering team and product stakeholders
## Nice to Have
• Experience with React Native tooling such as Expo, Metro, or React Native debugging tools
• Experience with mobile UI automation frameworks such as Detox, Maestro, or Appium (WebdriverIO)
• Experience with JavaScript/TypeScript testing tools such as Jest, Vitest, or React Native Testing Library
• Experience testing mobile apps on iOS and Android devices, simulators, and emulators (Xcode Simulator, Android Studio)
• Experience with Node.js servers or frameworks (e.g., Express, Fastify) and building or consuming REST APIs, WebSockets, or mock servers
• Experience with Git and basic version control workflows
• Familiarity with bug tracking and test management tools (e.g., Jira, TestRail)
• Familiarity with API tools like Postman
• Interest in or exposure to payments, POS systems, or hardware integrations
• Familiarity with CI/CD tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Bitrise, EAS)
## What You’ll Learn and Grow Into
• Designing a scalable React Native UI automation framework from the ground up
• Building mocks, simulators, and test fixtures for hardware and payment integrations in a production-quality Node.js and TypeScript codebase
• Understanding how React Native apps interact with native iOS and Android layers, and where platform-specific bugs come from
• Gaining hands-on exposure to debugging distributed systems, including tracing issues across services, understanding common failure modes, and learning proven solution approaches alongside our engineers
• Defining QA standards and best practices that the company will build on
• Shifting quality left by partnering with developers earlier in the development cycle
• Growing into a senior or lead quality role as the QA function expands, with the chance to help hire and onboard future team members
## What We Offer

AI has made writing code nearly free. Knowing whether that code, and the agents built on top of it, will behave in production hasn’t gotten any easier. Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.

About the Role
mpathic provides independent, multidisciplinary evaluations of healthcare AI technologies seeking deployment in real-world clinical settings. As part of our work supporting Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) regulatory sandbox, we are recruiting experienced machine learning (ML) and data science professionals to serve as technical reviewers on expert evaluation panels.
In this role, you will independently assess the technical evidence supporting healthcare AI applications, including model performance, validation methodology, generalizability, reliability, and proposed monitoring and safeguards. Your assessments will help inform recommendations regarding whether and under what conditions an AI technology may be appropriate for pilot deployment.
You will work alongside clinical and other subject-matter experts to evaluate whether applicants' technical claims are supported by credible evidence and whether their proposed evaluation and monitoring plans are appropriate for the intended healthcare setting and patient population.
This is an evaluation and scientific review role, not a model development position. We are looking for experts who can critically assess existing evidence, identify limitations, and communicate actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
What You'll Be Doing
Responsibilities may include:
• Evaluate model performance and validation: Assess the appropriateness of validation methods, reference standards, sample sizes, statistical analyses, performance metrics, operating thresholds, and reported uncertainty.
• Assess data quality and representativeness: Review whether training, testing, and validation datasets are appropriate for the intended clinical application, including potential data leakage, subgroup performance differences, and generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings.
• Evaluate technical reliability: Assess evidence of model robustness, reproducibility, known failure modes, and performance under atypical or out-of-distribution inputs.
• Review proposed evaluation plans: Determine whether applicants have established scientifically defensible methods, performance benchmarks, and success criteria for evaluating AI technologies during pilot deployment, particularly when pre-deployment evidence is limited.
• Assess technical safeguards and human oversight: Evaluate whether proposed technical safeguards, escalation mechanisms, and human-in-the-loop processes are operationally feasible and supported by appropriate testing.
• Evaluate monitoring and change management: Assess applicants' plans for detecting performance degradation, monitoring model behavior, managing updates, and establishing criteria for intervention or rollback.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary reviewers: Work alongside clinicians and other technical experts to identify concerns that require cross-disciplinary judgment, particularly where model performance may affect clinical outcomes.
• Produce structured evaluation findings: Document strengths, limitations, missing evidence, and technical concerns using a standardized review framework. Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations and identify what additional evidence or changes would resolve identified concerns.
• Participate in reviewer calibration and quality assurance: Contribute to discussions intended to improve consistency, transparency, and defensibility across evaluations.
• Maintain independence and confidentiality: Follow conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and data-handling requirements when reviewing proprietary or unpublished materials.
What We're Looking For
We are seeking technically rigorous, independent reviewers who can distinguish between a promising technology and evidence that adequately supports its proposed use.
Strong candidates are comfortable questioning unsupported performance claims, identifying limitations in study design, and recognizing when additional evidence is needed before meaningful conclusions can be drawn. They understand that healthcare AI evaluation is context-dependent: technical performance must be considered alongside the intended population, clinical application, degree of autonomy, and potential consequences of model error.
Candidates should also be able to translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for multidisciplinary audiences, including clinicians and state regulatory stakeholders.
Basic Qualifications
• At least 3 years of professional or applied research experience in machine learning, data science, biostatistics, clinical informatics, or a closely related field, with direct experience evaluating or validating predictive models or AI systems.
• Demonstrated understanding of model evaluation methodologies, including appropriate performance metrics, validation design, statistical uncertainty, threshold selection, and common sources of bias or methodological error.
• Experience assessing model performance on independent or held-out data and interpreting whether reported performance generalizes beyond the evaluation dataset.
• Hands-on experience evaluating at least one relevant class of AI systems, such as clinical natural language processing, large language models, conversational AI, medical imaging, computer vision, or tabular predictive models.
• Ability to critically assess technical research, evaluation reports, or validation studies and identify methodological limitations or unsupported conclusions.
• Strong analytical writing skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to work independently while contributing to multidisciplinary expert review and calibration processes.
• Willingness to complete confidentiality agreements, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and reviewer training requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience evaluating AI or ML systems used in healthcare, clinical decision support, digital health, or other high-stakes environments.
• Familiarity with clinical AI evaluation and reporting frameworks, such as TRIPOD+AI, STARD-AI, CONSORT-AI, DECIDE-AI, or model cards.
• Experience evaluating generative AI, LLM-based systems, or autonomous AI agents, including multi-turn behavior, reliability, hallucinations, and technical safeguards.
• Experience with robustness testing, adversarial evaluation, red teaming, or systematic failure-mode analysis.
• Knowledge of production monitoring, distribution shift, model drift, version control, and change-management practices.
• Experience designing or evaluating human-in-the-loop systems or comparing model performance against human expert judgments.
• Familiarity with FDA guidance for AI-enabled medical devices, clinical decision support, or software as a medical device.

## About Zact
Zact is a fintech innovator dedicated to helping organizations simplify expense and payment management. Our platform aligns employees, finance, and accounting with stronger controls, cleaner workflows, and continuous reconciliation to financial systems.
## Role Overview
The Product Owner, Integrated Payables is a hands-on product leader responsible for defining, prioritizing, and delivering Zact’s accounts payable and business payments product, which banks offer to their commercial customers.
Integrated Payables takes an invoice from receipt to reconciled payment: invoices arrive by email, upload, or payment instruction file (PIF); are OCR’d and coded; route through approvals; are paid on the best rail (virtual card, ACH, or check); and post back to the customer’s accounting system. The Product Owner owns that end-to-end experience and the backlog that drives it.
At Zact, this role combines two jobs that many companies split: Product Owner and Technical Product Manager (TPM). We do not use separate project managers. Our experience is that delivery is managed best by the person who knows the product most deeply, so the Product Owner owns both what gets built and how it gets delivered for Integrated Payables.
That means being on every sprint call with the engineering team, working with the Bank Delivery team to keep the backlog prioritized around what our banks need, constantly grooming the backlog, and personally driving features from requirement through release. We are looking for a working product owner who can get deep into AP and payments workflows, understand the technical design well enough to make real-time trade-offs, and keep delivery on track without handing it off to someone else.
The successful candidate will combine strong product judgment with technical fluency and a practical understanding of how payables actually work inside a finance team, and how banks and card processors deliver commercial payments. This person will help make Integrated Payables a compelling reason for banks to choose Zact and a meaningful driver of virtual card adoption and revenue.
## Key Responsibilities
## Product Ownership
• Build a deep understanding of Zact’s Integrated Payables product, the AP workflows of business customers, the bank distribution model, and the competitive landscape.
• Own the Integrated Payables product backlog and the product vision behind it, balancing bank commitments, revenue opportunities, technical debt, and long-term direction.
• Translate business needs into clear, well-structured user stories with detailed acceptance criteria, workflows, and edge cases that engineering can build against with confidence.
• Define and continually improve core payables capabilities, including invoice capture and OCR/AI extraction, PIF imports, GL coding, PO matching, approval workflows, and payment authorization.
• Drive the payment execution experience, including payment method prioritization across single-use and multi-use virtual cards, ACH, and check, with an emphasis on increasing card adoption.
• Own vendor-facing capabilities such as vendor enrollment, vendor portal, remittance advice, and supplier card acceptance programs.
• Ensure strong controls are built into the product, including role-based permissions, multi-factor authentication for sensitive actions, fraud prevention, and complete audit trails.
• Identify opportunities to apply AI and automation across the payables lifecycle to reduce manual effort for AP teams.
## Technical Delivery (TPM)
• Attend every sprint call for Integrated Payables, including stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint planning, sprint reviews, and retrospectives, as the engineering team’s day-to-day product partner.
• Own end-to-end delivery of Integrated Payables features: plan releases, track progress, manage dependencies, and identify and clear blockers before they affect timelines.
• Work with engineering on technical design, APIs, data flows, and integration approaches, and make informed scope and sequencing trade-offs in real time.
• Coordinate delivery across dependent teams and partners, including processors, card issuing and payment rails, accounting and ERP integrations, and QA.
• Manage delivery risks, issues, and changes to scope or timelines, and communicate status clearly to leadership, Bank Delivery, and sales.
• Accept completed work against acceptance criteria, lead user acceptance testing, and ensure releases meet a high standard of quality.
• Own release readiness, including release notes, product documentation, and enablement content for banks, sales, and customer success.
## Bank Delivery Partnership
• Work closely with the Bank Delivery team to understand each bank’s requirements, implementation timelines, and go-live commitments.
• Continually groom and reprioritize the backlog based on bank needs, ensuring commitments to banks are reflected in sprint plans and delivered on time.
• Participate in bank implementation discussions as the product expert, clarifying requirements, setting realistic expectations, and resolving product questions quickly.
• Triage bank-reported issues and enhancement requests with bank delivery and support and fold them into the backlog with clear priority.
• Engage directly with banks, business customers, sales, and implementation teams to gather feedback, validate solutions, and support demos and active opportunities.
• Establish practical product and delivery metrics, such as sprint predictability, on-time bank commitments, straight-through processing rates, and card payment mix, and use them to guide prioritization.
## Required Qualifications
## Product Ownership Experience
• 5+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or Business Analyst, ideally on B2B SaaS or fintech products.
• Demonstrated ability to write clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional requirements for complex workflows.
• Hands-on experience working in Agile/Scrum teams and leading backlog refinement, sprint planning, and sprint reviews.
• Comfort operating in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment where priorities evolve and initiative matters.
## Technical Product & Delivery Management
• Experience owning delivery end to end, as a Technical Product Manager, TPM, or Product Owner without dedicated project management support.

## About the role:
Cresta’s AI Receptionist answers the phone for small businesses that would otherwise miss the call. It handles millions of conversations a month today, making sure no call goes unanswered and helping owners complete the front-office tasks that keep their business running, and it does so across hundreds of customers. Whether those conversations are actually good is the single most important question in the business, and it deserves a full-time owner. That’s you.
As our first AI Agent Evaluation Engineer, you define what quality means for every agent we run, you build the systems that measure it across every conversation, and you are the person the company trusts when the question is “how good is it, really?”
The work combines hands-on conversation analysis, rigorous evaluation design, and engineering execution: reading and annotating real conversations to learn how the agent actually fails, building the automated evaluation systems (LLM-based judges, golden sets, regression suites) that measure those failures at scale, and keeping those systems honest by calibrating them against human judgment. Fixing what you find is welcome but not the core of the job; an accurate, prioritized picture of agent quality is.
What You'll Do :
## Evaluation Design & Quality Definition
• Define and maintain the evaluation rubric for the agent across three axes: adherence (did it follow its design, call the right tools, respect guardrails), outcome (did the conversation achieve its goal), and conversation experience (latency, turn-taking, tone, repetition).
• Write the annotation guidelines and failure taxonomy the team uses to talk about failures precisely; run calibration sessions and measure inter-rater agreement.
• Classify and prioritize failure modes by severity and frequency so engineering and product work on what matters most.
## Conversation Analysis & Annotation
• Review production conversations by hand every week, leverage QA partners; open-code failures, cluster them, and turn the clusters into the evaluations worth automating.
• Trace each failure to its likely cause (prompt, knowledge gap, tool or flow bug, speech recognition) and route it to the right owner with enough evidence to act on.
• Evaluate across languages and report quality by segment (language, accent, audio quality, intent), not just in aggregate.
## Scalable Evaluation Systems
• Build and operate the evaluation pipeline that scores every production conversation, combining automated checks, LLM-based judges, and human review.
• Calibrate every automated judge against human labels before trusting it; treat judge error as the primary measurement risk.
• Design sampling strategies (stratified by intent, language, caller type, audio conditions) so that reported changes in quality are real.
• Build and maintain the golden set and regression suite that every prompt, model, knowledge, and flow change is validated against before release.
## Coverage & Edge Cases
• Maintain the failure-mode coverage map: which behaviors are tested, partially tested, or unmeasured; close the gaps.
• Design evaluations for behaviors no standard harness covers: high-stakes conversation types such as handoffs to a human, misuse and unwanted-caller handling, and resilience under upstream failures.
• Define the quality and latency thresholds the agent is held to.
## Reporting & Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Report quality trends to internal stakeholders and customers clearly, with uncertainty stated and without burying bad news.
• Partner with forward-deployed engineers, backend engineers, product managers, and the voice/language engineering team to turn findings into prioritized recommendations.
• Document methodology so results are reproducible and the evaluation practice outlives any one person.
## What We're Looking For:
• 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, applied ML, or data-intensive research roles, including at least 1–2 years working hands-on with LLM-based systems in production.
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Built and operated an end-to-end evaluation system for a production LLM product (agent or otherwise): rubric, human labels, automated judge, regression suite.
• Deep understanding of evaluation methodology: what golden sets, judges, regression suites, and calibration are for, and when each fails. Tool-agnostic; you will work in our in-house tooling.
• Fluent in how LLM agents work: prompts, tool calls, context handling, multi-turn state. You can read a trace and tell what the agent was doing and why.
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with LLM APIs; able to build and ship evaluation tooling independently. Fine-tuning and ML frameworks are not required.
• Able to write a rubric that independent reviewers would score the same way, and to measure whether they do.
• Able to design a test from an open-ended quality question: you decide what to measure and how, rather than executing a predefined plan.
• Willing to do non-scalable work weekly, both yourself and by directing our QA partners: listening to calls, labeling conversations, building a failure taxonomy from scratch.
• Professional fluency in at least one language other than English, sufficient to evaluate multilingual agent behavior directly.
• Strong written communication; you author the guidelines others follow.

Nava is a consultancy and public benefit corporation working to make government services simple and effective. Since 2015, federal, state, and local agencies have trusted Nava to help solve highly scrutinized technology modernization challenges.
As a client services company, we guide agencies constrained by legacy systems to a future with sharp user experiences built on secure, reliable, fault-tolerant cloud infrastructure. We bill for our time, offering our expertise and problem-solving approach to help our government partners enhance their digital products and services. People are at the heart of our work, from members of the public who rely on benefit programs to government agency staff. Through human-centered design and modern engineering best practices, we help our government partners understand user needs and deliver on their missions more effectively. This focus gives everyone at Nava the opportunity to do work that is meaningful, impactful, and deeply connected to public good.

## Position summary
The Technical Trainer Lead prepares staff at a state workforce agency for each major launch milestone of Nava's paid family and medical leave benefits solution. They design and deliver role-based train-the-trainer sessions for the agency's claims adjudicators, appeals judges, contact center agents and supervisors, product owners, and leadership. It bridges the agency's business operations and Nava's technology teams to ensure the program works in practice for the people who use it.
The role has no direct reports and succeeds through influence rather than authority. It establishes training standards and templates for product managers and designers to follow, evaluates quality through readiness checks and accessibility and plain-language reviews, and escalates gaps to the Program Manager and Senior Program Manager. The role does not own the materials individual teams develop for their respective solutions, the Knowledge Base, the release calendar, or release go/no-go decisions.

• Design and deliver role-based train-the-trainer sessions built on real job scenarios, co-led with agency super-users from the first milestone
• Run a training sandbox (with a Nava engineer, using synthetic data) and run scripted readiness checks before each milestone; report readiness to Program Leadership on a metrics dashboard they design
• Set the templates and content standards (plain language, Section 508) that product managers and designers follow; update training after every release
• Hand over editable materials so the agency can keep training after Nava leaves
## Required skills
• 10 to 15+ years designing and delivering role-based training, including train-the-trainer, for government or other regulated operations staff
• Adult-learning instructional design built around real job tasks and scenarios
• Experience keeping training in step with agile releases or milestones
• Plain-language writing, plus training or certification in Section 508 accessibility
• Facilitation and influence skills; has led without direct authority
• Client-facing: bridges business operations and technology teams and represents the employer to stakeholders
