About Neo4j:
Neo4j is the graph intelligence platform that transforms data into knowledge to power the next generation of intelligent applications and AI systems. It includes enterprise-ready knowledge graphs for accurate, explainable, and governed AI; the most comprehensive, trusted, and easy-to-deploy graph capabilities across any environment and data source; and an unmatched ecosystem trusted by 84 of the Fortune 100 and supported by the world’s largest graph community. Intelligence that works. Results that matter.
Built to work everywhere and integrate with everything across every cloud for dynamic, personalized, and autonomous AI systems. We deliver quicker results, contextual knowledge, and solutions that impact customers and employees across the business.
Our Vision:
At Neo4j, we have always strived to help the world make sense of data.
As business, society and knowledge become increasingly connected, our technology promotes innovation by helping organizations to find and understand data relationships. We created, drive and lead the graph database category, and we’re disrupting how organizations leverage their data to innovate and stay competitive.
At Neo4j, our Solution Engineers are pivotal to our company’s success. As a member of our regional go-to-market team, you will partner with our sales executives, working closely with clients to showcase how the Neo4j Graph Intelligence Platform addresses their critical business needs. Neo4j Solution Engineers play a central, hands-on role as clients consider and evaluate Neo4j technology, and support customers in an advisory capacity throughout their journey to value realization. SE’s work with organizations across industries such as Financial Services, Telecommunications, Technology and Life Sciences understand the business and technical value of representing data using Neo4j graph database and analytics technology. You will grow as a thought leader in graphs and solve our customers’ high-value problems beyond traditional data solutions.
What Success Looks Like:
• Developing and honing subject matter expertise to effectively discern and understand the true needs of our customers, present technology solutions that target those needs, and all in all, demonstrate thought leadership and the value of Neo4j through platform and use case demonstrations, solution architecting, workshops, and conferences.
• Meeting and exceeding regional revenue goals, as a result of helping Sales to qualify and validate opportunities from a technical perspective and accelerate the sales cycle and adoption of Neo4j.
• Collaborating effectively with Sales, Professional Services, Partners, Product Management, etc to deliver continuous value to customers and ensure a seamless customer experience as they embark on the graph journey.
What You’ll Do:
• Confidently articulate the business and technical value of Neo4j to customers and prospects as a key technical advisor and advocate for our products and services
• Actively drive and run the technology evaluation stage of the sales cycles.
• Work across a number of opportunities in parallel and manage day-to-day activities such as opportunity qualification, technical discovery, presentations, platform and use case demonstrations, proof of value, sizing, and documentation of technical decision criteria.
• Build and nurture rapport with customer stakeholders at all levels and be the trusted advisor to them to help them understand what they can achieve with Neo4j.
• Co-create reference and solution architectures with our customers, including integrating Neo4j with their existing architecture and applications within a public cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP) or on-premise environment.
• Stay current on latest Neo4j capabilities, including but not limited to usage and integration with third-party tools and services.
• Distill and communicate customer needs and product feedback to Product Management, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales.
• Help drive demand through the participation in account-based marketing events as well as industry-known conferences and trade shows.
• Lead by example and actively foster an environment of teamwork, transparency, creativity, and continuous improvement.
• Travel as needed to assist in deal creation and closure, and provide support to your team as required.
What You’ll Bring:
• 5+ years of customer-facing experience in a similar capacity (Sales/Presales/Solutions Engineer, Solutions Architect, Technical Consultant, etc), ideally in a similar high-growth, scaling environment.
• Experience working with different data technologies in either of the following areas: enterprise data architecture, data analytics, data science or cloud data architecture.
• Familiarity with graph data technology is essential. Working knowledge of Neo4j is a strong plus!
• Hands-on experience and proficiency with relational (SQL) and/or NoSQL databases, and at least one of the following languages: Python, Java, JavaScript, Go, C#.
• Successful track record in designing, developing, and implementing data solutions in the public cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP) or on-premise.
• Ability to engage and communicate ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels through presentations, whiteboarding, and platform demonstrations.
• Technical savviness and business acumen to translate technical concepts and patterns into valuable business outcomes.
• Passion for learning new technologies (especially graphs!), developing new ways of data modeling, and spearheading change management.
• An entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to prioritize, pivot, and problem-solve.

• Build and maintain scalable automation suites using Playwright across web, API, and mobile, contributing to broader QA frameworks and release validation standards.

As a Quality Assurance Specialist embedded within our financial services practice, you serve as the final gatekeeper safeguarding digital communications before reaching broad customer audiences.
This role allocates approximately 80% of its scope to comprehensive Content QA—auditing creative assets from initial ideation through regulatory review, followed by rigorous testing within Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC), cross-client rendering environments, and live deployment validation to guarantee alignment with technical documentation, design specs, dynamic messaging logic, and WCAG standards.
The remaining 20% involves partnering with Technical QA Analysts to conduct data schema audits, HTML structure reviews, and deployment file verifications. • Assist with HTML code reviews: template use, link URLs, alt text, ARIA labels, heading structure, fonts, subject lines and preheaders.
• Review final file packages for completeness and naming conventions before hand-off to Salesforce.
• Help validate accessibility and logic fixes, and back up the Technical QA Analyst during peak periods.
## Team and Process
• Join internal creative reviews and developer handoffs to flag content and testing risks early.
• Attend daily scrum and weekly QA resource planning, and keep Workfront tasks and timesheets current.
• Contribute to retrospectives and help improve QA checklists, test plans and workflows.
What You Bring
## Experience & Expertise
• 2–4 years focused on editorial review, creative verification, or marketing quality assurance within client-facing agency networks or corporate environments.
• Direct operational experience validating responsive HTML communications, predominantly across Salesforce Marketing Cloud or equivalent enterprise campaign execution tools.
• Background supporting highly regulated sectors such as banking, insurance, or health, managing multi-tier governance workflows and legal sign-offs.
• Practical understanding of WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines, including alt tags, ARIA attributes, and semantic document markup.
• Proven history auditing real-time dynamic content and audience personalization against technical briefs, user criteria, and test scenarios.

## Skills & Capabilities

• Comfort with email render and testing tools such as Email on Acid, Litmus or Inbox Monster.
• Ability to use a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA or JAWS) to verify accessible content.
• Clear, concise written communication, especially bug reports that a developer can act on without a follow-up call.
• Strong organization and prioritization across several concurrent projects with shifting deadlines.
• Proficiency with Google Workspace and spreadsheets, for working with test plans, data files and change logs.
## Mindset
• Accountability: you own your QA sign-off and treat every missed error as a learning opportunity, not someone else's problem.
• Learning: you are curious about the technical side of email and eager to grow your skills toward Technical QA.
• Teamwork: you see QA as a partner to creative and development, not a gatekeeper, and you jump in when others are at capacity.
• Candor: you give direct, kind and specific feedback, and you ask questions early rather than assume.
• Composure: you stay calm and methodical during Live Testing crunches and same-day turnarounds, with compliance top of mind.

### **The Role**
SDVI’s SDETs set the test strategy for the projects they support. You’ll work with feature developers to agree on what needs to be true for us to ship with confidence, then design, build, and run the test infrastructure that proves it. The work centers on how Rally behaves as a system, under load, under failure, and in the ways customers use it, more than on how any one part is implemented. We don’t measure SDET by how many defects it finds. We measure whether the risk we accept at release is risk we chose.
As a Senior SDET, you’ll drive test strategy for a major project or area of Rally with minimal direction. You’ll shape the test infrastructure the rest of the team builds on, and help other SDETs and feature developers raise the quality of their tests.
### **What You’ll Work On**
• Implement test strategy with feature teams on a major project or area of Rally, and agree up front on what must be true for high-impact changes and who proves it
• Test Rally against defined system properties and invariants, especially those pertaining to scalability, resiliency, and performance at customer scale
• Design test infrastructure and fixtures that serve both test and development, weigh their tradeoffs with peers, and see them through implementation to adoption
• Build tests that return a clear verdict on well-defined system behaviors
• Advise feature developers as they own the development-loop tests for their own changes
• Test that Rally’s failures are diagnosable, so customers and support can tell what broke and why
• Review past production incidents with Support Engineering to find gaps in how we test
• Mentor other SDETs, and improve the practices and tools the team uses
### **What Success Looks Like**
• **First 90 days.** You’re shaping the test strategy for a major project, know the test infrastructure well enough to support and refine its design, and feature teams coordinate with you to ensure releases ship with confidence.
• **First year.** You drive test strategy for a major area of Rally and have defined and tested its system properties. Feature developers use fixtures you designed, and other SDETs come to you for guidance.

If you don’t meet every point above, we’d still like to hear from you.
### **How We Work**
• **We’re small and distributed.** Most of our collaboration happens over Slack and Zoom, across time zones. You’ll own what you build, and you’ll work closely with people outside your immediate team.
• **Engineers stay close to customers.** You’ll hear directly from the people using what you build. When something goes wrong in production, the team that owns the code helps fix it.
• **We dig for root causes.** When something breaks, we find out why instead of patching the symptom and moving on.

AI coding agents are part of how we work every day, and we invest in getting good at using them. We’re also careful with them, because customers run their content operations on Rally. We’re tracking industry trends and innovations, but using our day-to-day experiences to separate signal from noise.

This role leads day-to-day QA planning and execution, strengthens automation and regression coverage, coaches QA team members, and works closely with Product Owners and Engineering to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle rather than treating testing as a final-stage activity.
The QA Lead is expected to create clear visibility into test readiness, progress, risk, and blockers. The role owns the operating discipline of QA: defining test approaches, ensuring execution begins when planned, maintaining useful quality metrics, driving defect triage, and escalating issues early when delivery or release quality is at risk.

Quality Leadership & Accountability
• Own the day-to-day QA practice and establish consistent expectations for test planning, execution, documentation, and release readiness.
• Ensure QA work begins when planned and that delays, blockers, environment issues, data needs, or scope gaps are identified and communicated immediately.

• Hold QA team members accountable for execution commitments, timely updates, accurate status reporting, and follow-through.

Test Strategy, Planning & Execution

## Quality Engineer, Mobile, Audience Experience
About This Role
As a Quality Engineer at BibleProject, you empower teams to ship reliable, secure, and performant software by embedding quality practices throughout the development lifecycle. You lead with automation and observability, design for testability, and partner with Engineers, Product, and Design to shift quality left so that defects are prevented, not just detected. You'll design, build, and own the app's automation suite, identify where coverage is needed across the test pyramid and partner with engineers to close the gaps, and use production signals to target risk — bringing demonstrated experience driving quality for production software at scale.
The App squad owns the BibleProject mobile app, where our audience reads and studies Scripture, often in community. Quality is what makes that experience trustworthy, and mobile makes that its own kind of challenge: the app has to hold up offline or on a weak connection, across a wide range of iOS and Android devices. You'll be the quality owner and anchor for this squad, working independently and shaping how we build for quality early rather than waiting to be handed test cases. That matters especially right now: we're building toward the future of the app, and testability is still something we can shape as we go. Manual testing here is targeted exploratory discovery — the critical and edge cases, the accessibility gaps, the things automation won't catch — rather than high-volume regression.
Most importantly, you'll be an integral part of maturing the product engineering culture of BibleProject, setting and maintaining a high bar with regard to our standards and people, and working to create an environment where great technical professionals like yourself can ship work worthy of our mission at a sustainable pace that reflects the BibleProject values: creative, humble, thoughtful, unifying, generous, and unhurried.
Core Functions
Leadership
• Own the App squad's automation suite and quality roadmap independently — build, maintain, and evolve it without ongoing pairing support.
• Own test strategy across the pyramid: identify where tests are needed — unit, component, integration, end-to-end — and partner with engineers to close gaps, influencing scope and sequencing based on risk and user impact.
• Champion shift-left practices: drive testability in design reviews and codify quality engineering standards and patterns.
• Partner with Product, Design, DevOps, and Data to define testable acceptance criteria (usability, accessibility, offline/edge-case behavior) and align on SLOs and release readiness.
• Drive continuous improvement: identify bottlenecks in CI/CD, observability, and environments, and deliver measurable fixes.
Responsibilities
• Build and maintain the automation suite with durable patterns, stable test data, and reliable test environments across iOS and Android.
• Track coverage gaps as the product evolves, and partner with engineers to get unit and component-level tests written and maintained in the codebase.
• Integrate tests into CI/CD with clear gates, fast feedback, and actionable reporting, driving down flaky failures over time.
• Plan and execute targeted exploratory testing on critical flows, new designs, and edge cases — offline/poor-connectivity behavior, accessibility gaps, and other issues automation won't catch — documenting reproducible steps and user impact.
• Establish, track, and improve quality signals (defect rate, change-failure rate, test stability, coverage depth, crash-free rate); validate releases using production signals and lead post-release verification for high-risk launches.
Expertise
• Mobile test automation: hands-on building and maintaining mobile UI automation suites from durable, maintainable patterns rather than one-offs; experience with Appium and the Page Object Model is a plus.
• Observability and analysis: using logs, metrics, traces, and crash reporting to validate behavior and identify defects quickly.
• Mobile quality judgment: offline and poor-connectivity correctness, behavior across a wide device range, mobile performance budgets and their user impact, and the release constraints of shipping through app stores.
• Product fluency for mobile: fluent in iOS and Android conventions, able to identify and articulate why something that technically passes still violates expected user experience.
• UX, accessibility, and AI-assisted quality: practical accessibility techniques for mobile and qualitative usability methods, plus comfort using AI-assisted tools to generate test ideas and data, summarize signals, and draft reports with human review and privacy-safe handling.
What We're Looking For
• 5+ years of experience (or equivalent skill) building and maintaining automated tests and quality tooling in a product team, including production software at scale.
• Demonstrated ability to build and own a mobile automation suite independently — designing stable tests, integrating them into a delivery pipeline, and driving down flakiness — without ongoing pairing support.
• Track record of risk-based coverage analysis: identifying where tests add the most value across a product and partnering with engineers to close gaps.
• Proven experience using production signals and observability to guide testing strategy and risk mitigation.
• Demonstrated ability to translate usability, accessibility, and performance expectations into testable acceptance criteria.
• Track record of surfacing blockers early and driving them to resolution without recurring escalation.
• Track record of giving and incorporating feedback, with demonstrated growth in scope of ownership over time.
• Alignment with BibleProject's mission and values.

Portland, Oregon, Founded in 2014
BibleProject is an educational technology and media studio whose mission is to help people experience the Bible as a unified story that leads to Jesus.
We have grown significantly in the area of multimedia technology. What began with two animated videos now encompasses multiple platforms and products—including over 200 videos. Our website and app serve as connection hubs to our ever-growing library of resources. Classroom, our online learning platform, offers accessible, graduate-level Bible classes.
These, and all of our supporting products, continue to be completely free to audiences around the world, thanks to the ongoing generosity of our patrons.

Use AI coding agents and related tools to explore the SDK codebases, understand behaviour and accelerate quality work.

Design, build and maintain useful unit and component tests for SDK behaviour.

Put automated tests into active CI and release workflows, with failures that are clear and actionable.

Investigate bugs using code, logs, APIs, test results and product behaviour.

Work with builders to improve testability and prevent repeated classes of defects.
Turn repeated investigation or testing work into reusable AI workflows, tools, checks or test assets.

You will be succeeding when:
Important SDK behaviours have dependable automated protection;
Useful quality improvements land incrementally and are easy for the team to adopt;
SDK-to-platform integration failures are detected early and are easy to diagnose;
Tests run reliably in the workflows the team actually uses;

## About Supermove
Supermove builds software and AI for moving companies. We've raised $30M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors. We started in 2019 as the system that runs a moving business: sales, operations, crews, billing. Today that system runs moving companies across the US, Canada and Australia, from single-location movers to some of the largest van lines and franchise systems in North America.
Now we're putting AI to work on top of it. Our voice agents answer and call leads, book moves, and hand off to a person at the right moment. Autopilot, our agent platform, goes further. It answers questions about the business in plain language, flags what needs attention, and handles work that used to take a person's whole day, from working the inbox to updating jobs.
## The role
Every moving company runs on its own logic: its own rates and tariffs, its own way of paying crews and commissioning salespeople, its own accounting system, and often a van line with rules of its own. When a customer signs, someone has to turn all of that into a working Supermove account. That's you.
You'll own implementations from kickoff to go-live and a clean handoff to our customer success team, running several at once. On our largest accounts, you'll work alongside a Key Account Director who owns the relationship and the results. You own the build.
This is a hands-on role. You won't write requirements and hand them to someone else. You'll be inside Supermove every day, configuring, testing, and tracing why an invoice or a sync came out wrong. The people who love this job would rather be in the tool than reporting on it.
## What you'll do
Run implementations from kickoff to go-live: discovery, configuration, testing, training, launch. Set the dates and hold the customer and our team to them.
Turn how a customer charges and pays into working configuration: pricing and tariffs, billing formulas, hourly minimums, crew pay, and salesperson and contract-driver commissions.
Design account structures for multi-location companies and franchise systems, and build master templates that dozens or hundreds of locations can start from.
Set up and fix accounting integrations. Map the general ledger, get invoices and vendor bills flowing to Sage Intacct or QuickBooks, and help the customer's finance team reconcile.
Connect customers to their van lines (Unigroup, SIRVA and others) so orders, statements and settlements flow without retyping.
Set up voice agents and Autopilot workflows with the customer. Decide where the AI acts on its own and where a person signs off, then listen to real calls and fix what's failing.
Use AI agents to do the work faster: investigating issues, drafting configuration, working through data, answering customer questions. Then help define what our own configuration and Autopilot agents should do next.
Turn what customers run into into clear bug reports and product requests, with screenshots and the customer's own words, and follow them through with engineering.
Train customer teams, from office staff to crews, around how they'll actually use the system, not a generic tour of features.
Improve how we implement. Own the templates, checklists, QA and handoff steps, and teach new team members.
## What this role asks of you
Comfort with how money moves. You know what a general ledger, AP and AR, a vendor bill and a reconciliation are, and you can talk to a controller in their language.
Logic and formulas. You can turn a commission sheet or a rate contract into rules a system can run, and spot the case that breaks them.
Comfort ahead of the documentation. We're putting AI into an industry that's never had it, so there's often no runbook yet. You'll design the approach while running it, then write it down so the next implementation starts further ahead.
AI as a working tool. You already use AI to get more done, not as a novelty. Candidates who've built it into how they work stand out.
Patience with a low-tech user base. Dispatchers, sales reps, and owners who've run the same way for twenty years. Changing how they work takes credibility on the ground as much as a project plan.
## What we're looking for
5+ years implementing or configuring complex business software (ERP, accounting, payroll, field-service, or vertical SaaS) for customers, owning the go-live. Experience with field-heavy businesses like construction, home services, fleet or logistics is a plus.
Accounting or bookkeeping experience is a big plus.
Technical enough to troubleshoot. You understand APIs, webhooks and data syncs well enough to tell where something broke. SQL or light scripting is a plus.
You've run several projects at once without dropping any, and you can tell us how.
Clear and steady with customers, whether you're training a dispatcher or telling a controller why the numbers don't match yet.
You write clearly. A lot of this job happens in writing.
Moving, van-line or relocation experience is a plus. We'll teach you the industry.
## Why this role matters
A moving company trusts us with how it quotes, bills, pays its people and closes its books. If implementation gets that right, everything built on top of it works, AI included. You'll shape how we implement as we grow into larger and more complex customers, and how our own AI agents take on more of this work.

It answers questions about the business in plain language, flags what needs attention, and handles work that used to take a person's whole day, from working the inbox to updating jobs.
## The role
We're hiring a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer to help build and lead our Forward Deployed Engineering function alongside Supermove's founders.
Our largest customers operate hundreds of locations, with thousands of employees, complex workflows, and multiple systems that need to work together. Getting AI to work reliably inside these businesses is a hard engineering problem. That's where you come in.
You'll work directly with our largest customers to understand how their businesses operate, build and deploy AI solutions, and make sure they deliver real results. This isn't a role where you hand requirements to engineering and wait for someone else to build them. You'll write production code, improve our AI agents, build integrations, and solve technical problems yourself.
You'll also work closely with our product and engineering teams to turn what you learn in the field into improvements to the core platform. The goal isn't to build a different solution for every customer. It's to figure out what works, make it reusable, and help us scale it.
As one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers, you'll work directly alongside the founders to define how this function operates, from the technical tools and deployment processes to how we hire and develop the team over time.
## What you'll do
Build and lead the FDE function. Work alongside the founders to establish the engineering practices, tooling, and processes for deploying AI at enterprise scale. Help shape and grow the team as we expand.
Ship production code. Build and improve AI agents, integrations, and core product capabilities. Work directly in our codebase to solve customer problems and improve the platform.
Lead technical deployments for major accounts. Own the technical execution from discovery and solution design through implementation, testing, go-live, and ongoing improvement. Work across engineering, product, and customer teams to get things done.
Design AI solutions for real operations. Understand how a customer works and determine how our Voice Agents and Autopilot should fit into their business, including where AI can take action and where people need to stay involved.
Make AI agents work reliably. Review calls and agent sessions, investigate failures, improve prompts and workflows, fix underlying code, and measure performance in production.
Turn customer problems into product improvements. Identify patterns across deployments and build reusable capabilities rather than one-off solutions. Help shape the technical roadmap based on what customers actually need.
Deliver measurable results. Make sure what you build works in production and creates real value for customers. Use data to understand performance, identify problems, and demonstrate impact.
## What we're looking for
4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping production systems.
Strong full-stack or backend engineering skills. You're comfortable working across APIs, databases, integrations, and complex application logic.
Experience building with LLMs, AI agents, or AI-powered workflows. You understand the challenges of making probabilistic systems work reliably in production.
You've owned technically complex projects end to end, from understanding the problem and designing a solution to writing code, deploying it, and making sure it works.
You're comfortable working directly with customers. You can explain technical tradeoffs to a CEO or COO and work with frontline operators to understand how their business actually runs.
You can lead without needing a large team or formal authority. You're comfortable coordinating engineers and other stakeholders, making decisions, and driving work forward.
You thrive in ambiguity. You don't need a perfectly defined spec to get started, and you're willing to dig into unfamiliar systems to figure out how things work.
You use AI seriously in your own work and are constantly experimenting with new tools and approaches to build faster and better.
Moving, logistics, or field-services experience is a plus. We'll teach you the industry.
## Why this role matters
We're at the beginning of bringing AI into some of the largest moving companies in North America. These businesses have complicated operations, and making AI work inside them requires more than building a good model or a polished demo.
You'll be one of the first engineers responsible for bridging that gap. You'll work directly with customers, build production AI systems, and help determine how we turn successful deployments into a scalable product.
You'll also work alongside Supermove's founders to build a new engineering function from the ground up, with significant influence over its technical direction, how it operates, and the team we build around it.
You'll have the opportunity to build the product, lead real-world deployments, and help shape the engineering team that brings AI into an entire industry.
## Process
Intro call → technical interview → practical engineering exercise → founder interview.

Twingate is building a modern remote access solution that simplifies and improves the way businesses secure access to their cloud, SaaS, and on-prem resources. Twingate is backed by leading investors such as BOND, WndrCo, 8VC, Green Bay Ventures, SignalFire, and Dropbox founders Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi. Our investors share our belief that in a world where workforces are becoming increasingly distributed, it is critical to be able to effectively secure access to apps, data, and environments.
As part of our company culture, our belief in putting the customer first permeates our thinking in everything from our customer communications to the design process behind the product itself. If you take pride in creating experiences with the customer firmly at the center of the picture, we'd love to work with you.
## About Twingate
For thirty years, securing access to a company's systems has meant making them harder to use. The VPN is the clearest example: a tunnel into the whole network, slow for the people who need it and trusted far more than it deserves. The industry's answer has been more layers and more acronyms. We think that is the wrong direction.
Twingate exists to prove that the most secure way to do something can also be the easiest. A user opens their laptop and the application is simply there. Behind that, every connection is checked against who the person is, what device they are on, and what they are allowed to reach, and nothing else is visible. Security people do not have to think about is the only kind that actually gets used.
We sell to IT and security teams, and increasingly to engineers: some companies embed Twingate inside their own products and platforms. From startups to large enterprises, the deal is won or lost on whether the product does what we say in the customer's real environment. That is where Solutions Engineering lives. Our customers say it better than we do: twingate.com/customers.
## The role
Most solutions engineers are measured on whether the demo went well. You will be measured on whether the technical evaluation produced a decision, and on making that decision a success for the customer.
You own the technical journey for our largest and most complex opportunities, from discovery through technical close and into production. Your job is to make sure the customer ends up with what they actually need, which is rarely what they first asked for, and that the people who championed Twingate internally are proven right for having done so.
Everyone on our team takes it personally when a customer does not get real value from what we build. We want someone who shares that mindset: the kind of person who opens doors for others without expecting a thank you, and who keeps asking what a customer experience could look like if nobody had done it that way before. Our shorthand for it: good service is giving champagne when asked. Great service is giving champagne at the right moment, before being asked.
## Responsibilities
Run technical evaluations that end in a decision. You and the customer agree in writing, before the work starts, on what success looks like and which requirements are deal-breakers. You keep that agreement current, call it early when a deal-breaker cannot be met, and separate what the evidence shows from what you were told.
Qualify properly, including out. Before you propose anything, you know why the customer should do anything at all, why now, and who cares. You turn vague terms into testable behavior, pull on every thread of a multi-part answer instead of acknowledging it and moving on, and find the driver behind the request rather than the solution the customer proposed. People are good at normalizing pain; you do not take "we don't have much" at face value. When we are not the right fit, you say so early.
Find and build technical champions. Behind every Twingate deployment is someone who put their credibility on the line to bring us in. Your job is to make that person successful: anticipate what they will need before they ask, give them what they need to make the case internally, and make sure the win is theirs. You give more than you get, every time.
Go deep when it is needed, and know when it is not. You can go as deep as any engineer in the room needs, and you can explain the same idea to someone who has never opened a terminal. The skill is reading the composition of the audience and adjusting automatically, so that nobody is left behind and nobody is bored. You are the customer's primary educator, and you are intentional about delivering value to every person on the call regardless of their technical background.
Leave the team better than you found it. Your trackers, guides, demo environments, and product feedback are built so others can use them without you in the room. You give teammates direct feedback on their qualification. And the relationship does not end at the signature: you stay directly involved through onboarding once a prospect becomes a customer, because the person who ran the evaluation is the person who knows what was promised. Continuity matters to us.
## Qualifications
• 8+ years in a customer-facing technical role, including several on enterprise deals with multiple technical stakeholders.
• Technical evaluations you scoped and ran yourself that ended in a clear win or a clear, early disqualification.
• Practical networking knowledge: how TCP and UDP connections are established, how DNS resolves, how TLS authenticates two parties, what NAT does to a packet, and ideally how to read a packet capture.
• Hands-on with at least one major cloud, Kubernetes, and an identity provider such as Okta, Entra ID, or Google Workspace. Endpoint security and device management tools (CrowdStrike, Intune, Jamf) are a strong plus.
• Scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell, and working with REST and GraphQL APIs. Enough to automate a test or build a small integration, not to ship software.
• A structured qualification method (MEDDPICC or similar). We care less which one and more whether you can show us yours from a real deal.
• Clear, succinct writing. Most of the value in this role is written.
• Familiarity with zero trust network access and adjacent categories helps but is not required. We can teach the market; we cannot teach intellectual curiosity.
## How You Work
These traits predict success in this role better than anything on the list above.
Driven by customer value. You measure yourself by whether the customer is better off, not by whether the deal closed. You go out of your way for people who may never know you did; you welcome credit but do not particularly thrive on it.
Resilient. Deals stall, champions leave, evaluations fail for reasons outside your control. You rebound on your own and are comfortable being uncomfortable.
Emotionally intelligent. You read a room from what people do, not only what they say: the stakeholder who has checked out, the champion under pressure, the "yes" that is a polite no.
Coachable

## Description
SAIC is seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) to join the Joint Range Extension (JRE) software development team.
This is a REMOTE ROLE within the UNITED STATES. MUST BE A U.S. CITIZEN. This role will involve up to 10% of CONUS travel.
JRE is a combat-proven data link gateway that plays a vital role in the defense of the United States and our allies by extending the reach of tactical data across the battlespace and around the globe. It is a large, mission-critical, near-real-time system written predominantly in Java and Kotlin, and also includes C++ components. JRE is deployed everywhere from handheld devices and small-form-factor drones to strategic bombers, guided-missile destroyers, and global command-and-control centers.
As a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) on the software development team, you'll work closely with other developers, as well as with testers and test engineers on the test team. Through test automation, you'll play an essential role in enabling rapid, agentically-developed, high-quality releases of JRE to meet the current and future mission needs of the warfighter.
Your impact will extend beyond the code you write yourself. You'll lead projects and build up the test engineering skills of the people you work with.
JOB DUTIES:
• Expand JRE's unit, integration, service, GUI, and end-to-end test automation .
• Engineer and maintain a comprehensive automated performance test suite covering load, stress, and endurance testing; support our IT team with capacity planning for the hardware environment it requires.
• Design, develop, and maintain advanced simulators for IP and serial tactical data link terminals, radios, navigation systems, and sensors.
• Contribute to the definition and ongoing verification of minimum system requirements for JRE's full range of deployment platforms.
• Refactor JRE code for testability, introducing API, RPC, and messaging seams to enable additional white- and gray-box testing.
• Mentor developers, testers, and less-experienced test engineers in test automation best practices as we expand automated coverage across the codebase.
• Optimize the performance and quality of our test automation suites.
• Quarantine, troubleshoot, and fix nondeterministic tests.
## Qualifications
Required Education:
• Bachelor's degree and nine (9) years’ experience; additional four (4) years’ experience can be considered in lieu of degree.
Required Clearance:
• Must have the ability to obtain and maintain an active Secret security clearance; US Citizenship required.

We are looking for an early-career systems engineer who likes figuring out what a system actually needs to do and then proving that it does. You’ll sit down with the operators who use DoD mission systems every day, turn what they tell you into clear, testable requirements, and write the test procedures that operators and developers use to verify each release. Just as important, you’ll explain why a request should or shouldn’t be built, and stand behind that recommendation. Our purpose is singular — to optimize warfighter performance
through information technology.
We hire for talent and drive over years on a résumé. Strong recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
You have…
• A clear, structured voice. You can walk someone through a problem — the situation, the options you weighed, what you decided, and the result so operators, engineers, and leaders follow it the first time.
• A curious mind. You want to understand how a system is really used, not just how it was designed.
• A good ear and good judgment. You listen for what operators need versus what they ask for, weigh it against technical constraints and the backlog, and can tell a customer “not now” while pointing them to a better path.
• An ownership mindset. When something is blocked, you go find the person who can unblock it instead of waiting.
• A dedication to detail. A vague requirement becomes a bug or a dispute later, so you pin it down now.
• A focus on the craft. You want to go deep in systems engineering and software requirements, test, and how software actually gets built.
• An open mind. You welcome feedback on your work and want to grow as an engineer.
We have…
• A devotion to making technology work for the warfighter. We help operators work faster, better, and smarter.
• An affinity to action. We’d rather start, learn, and iterate than wait for the perfect plan.
• A drive for continuous improvement. We look for better ways to solve old problems, for our customers and ourselves.
• Senior engineers who mentor. You’ll learn requirements and test practice alongside experienced test leads and SMEs.
What you’ll do…
Requirements elicitation and decomposition
Run discovery with operators, subject matter experts, and government leads, through interviews, site visits, and demos, to understand mission workflows, pain points, and what would make a capability acceptable to them.

• Trace requirements across subsystems and interfaces (APIs, data exchanges, connected systems) and assess the ripple effect of each change.
• Capture non-functional requirements (the “-ilities”): performance, reliability, security, and operation in degraded or disconnected (DDIL) conditions.
• Maintain requirements traceability from source (operator input, PWS, user stories) through design and test.
Operator input and prioritization
• Capture every operator or customer request as a data point: log it in the backlog, link it to existing requirements, and track it to a decision.
• Weigh requests against mission value, technical constraints, and the existing backlog; recommend build, defer, or decline, and explain why.
• Reconcile conflicting inputs from different operators or stakeholders and bring a recommended resolution to the team.
• Close the loop with operators on what was decided and when.
Documentation
• Document requirements, use cases, and operational workflows in formats operators and developers both understand.
• Write user stories with measurable acceptance criteria, including Given-When-Then (Gherkin) scenarios.
• Use quick prototypes or mockups (including AI-assisted ones) to confirm intent with operators and show developers the target outcome, without dictating how they build it.
• Produce supporting artifacts: workflow and system diagrams, Technical Exchange Meeting (TEM) minutes, and test reports.
Test planning and execution
• Write step-by-step test procedures and scripts that operators and developers can follow to verify functionality.
• Execute and support functional, regression, integration, and user acceptance testing (UAT) for software releases.
• Record results, log defects with clear reproduction steps, and verify fixes.
• Help automate repeatable testing: write simple scripts for test data and log checks, turn manual procedures into automated test cases and BDD step definitions.
• Contribute to functional security test cases (authentication, access control).
Collaboration
• Work alongside developers, test leads, cybersecurity staff, and program management in an Agile environment.
• Coordinate across multiple organizations and drive communication plans that keep responses and deliverables on schedule.
• Participate in sprint planning, TEMs, and customer reviews; brief findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
• Help developers reproduce and isolate defects by reading logs and tracing system behavior to narrow the root cause.
• Contribute technical writing to proposals as opportunities arise.
## Requirements
• 0–4 years of experience in systems engineering, requirements analysis, software testing, or quality assurance. Internships, co-ops, and capstone projects count.
• Hands-on work on a software project (professional, academic, or personal) where you can clearly describe the product, the team’s roles, and your part in it.
• Experience gathering requirements from end users or stakeholders and writing them as clear, testable. statements with measurable acceptance criteria.
• Experience writing test cases or test procedures and executing functional or regression testing.
• Basic debugging skills: reproducing an issue, reading logs or error output, and narrowing down the cause.

test data setup or log parsing.

## About Practifi (The Real Story)
Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.
That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.
## The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)
When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.
Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.
We're creating this role to change that. As our Data QA Analyst, you'll be the dedicated owner of data migration quality across every client onboarding engagement. You'll work the checklist object by object, build one standard the whole team uses, and spot the patterns a single-project view misses. You'll be a big part of why a client's first login feels like their business, not a spreadsheet import.
## Your Day-to-Day (The Honest Version)
The Core Work
• Validate every migration end to end. You'll analyze source data (record counts, missing values, duplicates, orphaned contacts, inconsistent values), then walk through the Practifi interface object by object to confirm everything displays and connects the way the client's Data Mapping Document says it should.
• Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
• Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
• Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
• Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
• Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.
The Reality Check
The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.
You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.
The Growth
This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.
You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. We promote from within. A role that sees every engagement is a strong foundation for a path into consulting, data engineering, or delivery leadership.
## What We're Really Looking For
The Must-Haves
• 3 to 5 years of experience in data quality, data migration, data validation, or quality assurance, ideally in a CRM or software environment
• Hands-on experience reconciling data: comparing record counts, running field-by-field checks, and finding duplicate and orphaned records
• Comfort working inside Salesforce or a comparable CRM, navigating objects, records, and related lists
• A working understanding of how relational data fits together (IDs, lookups, and records that link other records)
• Experience logging and tracking issues in JIRA, Asana, or a similar tool
• Clear written communication, including findings a non-technical stakeholder can act on
The Nice-to-Haves
• Experience with Salesforce Inspector, the Salesforce Developer Console, Data Loader, or SOQL queries
• Background in wealth management, financial services, or another regulated industry
• Experience supporting client onboarding or software implementation projects
• Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivot tables, conditional formatting)
A Salesforce certification isn't required to apply. You'll earn one with us.
The More Important Stuff
• You’re observant and tuned into the details within the data.
• You care about the cause of an issue, not just the fix.
• You're comfortable telling a Project Manager something they don't want to hear, and you do it early and kindly.
• You like building structure where there isn't any yet.
• You're honest about what you don't know and curious enough to go find out.
## What Taking This Leap Gets You
The Practical Stuff
• Base salary: $78,000 to $95,000. We share the range because you deserve to know it before you apply. Where you land depends on your experience against the role.
• Generous time off: 20 days of paid vacation, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 3 volunteering days annually
• Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance benefits, plus a 401(k) with company match
• Fully remote within the US
The Cultural Stuff
• A Practibuddy mentor from your first day, so you always have someone to ask
• An annual Learnbucks education stipend for the courses and certifications you choose
• Bi-annual in-person summits in Chicago where the whole company gets together
• A Slack culture where questions are welcome and wins get celebrated
• Remote-first that's real: genuine work-life integration, not a line in a job ad
## Living Our Values Daily
• Growth: You'll be part of building a function from the ground up, with Learnbucks and a real promotion path behind you.
• Collaboration: You'll partner with every delivery role on every engagement, and the fix is always a team effort.
• Transparency: The salary is in this ad, and your QA findings will be shared openly, good news and bad.

## Job Description
About the role
The Leader of Product Operations builds the operating system that helps Xplor use AI responsibly, adopt it widely, and turn it into revenue and contribution margin, with clear governance and accountability for the results. The role covers three connected areas: AI-enabled productivity, adoption of AI features by our customers, and the commercialization of those features. You will own the shared layer that makes all three work including measurement, value tracking, portfolio governance, intake, cost visibility, and the operating cadence that keeps leaders aligned.
Our products and teams span a wide mix of tools and workflow methodologies. You will create a shared layer of measurement, visibility and improvement that works across them, and that product, engineering, go-to-market and executive leaders all trust, and speeds teams up without creating friction.
You will report to the Chief AI Officer and partner closely with BU presidents, product and R&D leaders, GTM, Finance, Security, Legal, Privacy and the People team. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will build the function and stay close to the data and the teams.
How we work: BUs are central's customers. We measure outcomes, not activity. We decide on a demo, an eval or a metric, not a deck. We keep forums and reporting to the minimum that supports a real decision.
What you'll do
Own the measurement and board scorecard
• Build and run a single scorecard with Finance that records every AI benefit, in one engine, net of AI cost (inference, hosting, tools and support).
• Produce the quarterly AI board scorecard covering value and risk measures, with a named owner and source system for every measure.
• Run a repeatable prioritization and triage process for operations and tooling improvements, with clear owners, expected impact and follow-up on results.
• Turn data into short, decision-ready narratives for the Chief AI Officer and C-suite.
Measure AI-enabled productivity
• Build a measurement framework that links delivery and AI-SDLC productivity signals (cycle time, throughput, quality, adoption of AI tooling) to business outcomes such as idea-to-customer lead time, PR-to-production rate, change failure rate, escaped defects, rework and capacity moved to customer-facing work.
• Help leaders see where AI productivity gains are real, where they are not, and where to invest next.
• Act as a neutral orchestrator across teams that use different tools and methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe-style and hybrids; Jira, Azure DevOps and others), meeting each team where it is.
• Find where gains stall before reaching customers (review wait, regression coverage, late QA, launch readiness) and route the fix.
• Partner with function owners in support, revenue operations, finance and onboarding to baseline target workflows on fully loaded cost per resolved outcome, with quality held constant.
Measure AI product adoption and commercialization
• Own the metrics and standardize reporting for how customers adopt and use AI features across the portfolio at 30-60-90 days, from activation and usage depth to retention and satisfaction.
• Build the commercial view with Finance and BU leaders: AI and data ARR, paid attach, retention and expansion, win-rate uplift, gross margin per AI feature and cost per successful task.
• Run the launch-readiness checklist with BU leaders before any AI price goes live: cost per task known, margin target met after inference, attribution rule and holdout set, sales and customer success enablement ready.
Govern Data and AI accountability
• Operationalize and maintain decision rights, escalation paths and clear ownership for data and AI initiatives, so every investment has a named accountable owner, success measures, and a review date.
• Maintain a portfolio-level register of Data and AI initiatives and risks, and surface issues early to the Chief AI Officer with recommended actions.
• Run the Data and AI vendor and partner inventory and monthly review with Procurement, Finance and Security: spend, overlap, security review, data terms and knowledge transfer from consultants.
• Track adherence to agreed standards and policies, and report exceptions without becoming a bottleneck for teams.
Lead the function
• Hire, develop and lead a product operations team, and set its mandate, operating model and success measures.
• Apply AI to product operations itself, including automated reporting, insight synthesis and workflow automation.
## Qualifications
What you'll bring
Required
• 8+ years in product operations, business operations, strategy and operations, technical program management, product management, or a similar role in a SaaS or technology company, with at least 3 years at a senior or director level.
• A track record of building KPI and measurement frameworks that connect product or delivery data to business outcomes such as adoption, retention and revenue.
• Experience working with Finance, Sales and Marketing on pricing, packaging, launch or go-to-market performance.
• Experience leading cross-functional initiatives across Product, Engineering, Customer Success and executive leadership, and influencing without direct authority, including establishing governance, decision rights and accountability mechanisms that teams actually follow.
• Working knowledge of multiple delivery methodologies (Agile, Scrum, Kanban, SAFe) and the ability to support teams that use different ones.
• Hands-on fluency with product and delivery tooling (Jira or similar), product analytics, BI and data integration across systems.
• Strong written and verbal communication, including presenting data and tradeoffs clearly to executives.
• Experience building or leading a team, including hiring and coaching.
Preferred
• Experience with product adoption, monetization, or usage-based pricing.
• Experience measuring the impact of AI-assisted development or other engineering productivity programs, including frameworks such as DORA and SPACE.
• Experience in vertical SaaS or a multi-product portfolio, including products at different stages of modernization.
• Comfort using AI tools and automation in your own daily operating workflow.
• Experience with governance, risk classification or responsible-AI programs, working alongside Security, Legal and Privacy.
• Experience managing a vendor and partner portfolio, including consolidation and contract standards.
• Experience with cloud or AI cost management (FinOps): unit economics, cost per task.
Success Measurement
• First 30 Days: Inventory of AI tools, vendors, spend, pilots and production systems complete. Baseline scorecard and product readiness cards published. Steering cadence and decision log running.
• 60 Days: Board scorecard reported on its first full quarter in partnership with FinOps and BU leaders. Cost visibility by BU and product in place. Adoption and cost per task tracked for every live AI pilot. Stage gates in use for new initiatives.

## Meet the Team
Our team is part of the Cisco AI and Automation portfolio, responsible for the "Circuit" platform—the central AI engine that powers productivity and process automation for all of Cisco. We are a rapidly expanding, high-impact group dedicated to building the vehicle for AI-driven business transformation. We operate at the intersection of applied research and production, ensuring our technology is not only cutting-edge but also optimized for performance, reliability, and functional quality for our 80,000+ monthly users.
As an Automation QA Engineer, you are the guardian of that functional quality—owning the automated testing ecosystem that keeps Circuit reliable, scalable, and production-ready across every release. This is a hybrid position.
## Your Impact
As an Automation QA Engineer , you will drive the transformation of our regression testing ecosystem, moving beyond manual processes to build AI-driven, fully automated test suites for both new and legacy features. You will design and own end-to-end (E2E), API, and performance test automation that ensures the Circuit platform continues to meet Cisco's high standards for functional quality and performance.
You will build and maintain scalable test frameworks, integrate them into CI/CD pipelines for continuous quality feedback, and leverage AI-assisted coding tools (such as Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) to generate and maintain tests—while rigorously validating that AI-generated artifacts are stable, correct, and compliant with security standards. This is a high-visibility role where your ability to automate functional quality and reduce technical debt directly ensures Circuit remains a reliable vehicle for process automation across Cisco.
## Responsibilities
Automated Regression & E2E Testing: Architect, build, and maintain comprehensive automated regression and end-to-end test suites for the entire Circuit platform using Playwright (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python/Pytest , and Selenium, replacing manual QA with scalable automation.
API Testing: Design and automate REST and GraphQL API test suites covering functional correctness, contract validation, error handling, and performance—including validation of AI/model-serving endpoints under concurrent load.
Performance & Load Testing: Plan and execute load, stress, and soak tests using k6 or JMeter, ; track response-time percentiles (p95/p99), throughput, error rates, and AI-specific metrics such as Time to First Token (TTFT) and inter-token latency.
AI-Driven Test Automation: Use AI agents and AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code) to generate and maintain regression suites for new and legacy features; read and judge the stability of auto-generated code and ensure it does not violate security standards before it is merged.
AI Application & Agent Validation: Develop testing approaches for AI/LLM features—validating model response quality, behavior consistency (stability testing), and end-to-end AI agent workflows across both the reasoning and action layers.
CI/CD Integration & Reporting: Integrate all automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or equivalent) for continuous validation; build dashboards and reports (Grafana, Allure) and communicate quality metrics, risk assessments, and defect trends to engineering leadership.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Act as a "Team Captain" for automation initiatives—defining standards, mentoring peers, and collaborating with development, product, and UX teams to embed automation-first testing into the core development lifecycle.
## Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree with 4+ years, Master's degree with 3+ years, or PhD with 1+ year of related experience in Computer Science, AI/ML, or a related technical field.
• Experience in test automation and regression framework development , with a deep understanding of functional quality assurance.
• Experience with Playwright (TypeScript/JavaScript) for E2E/UI automation and/or Python with Pytest /Robot Framework; familiarity with Selenium.
• Experience with REST API testing (and familiarity with API contract testing); GraphQL testing a plus.
• Solid conceptual and practical knowledge of software development lifecycles, including CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar) and automated testing best practices.
• Experience in AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code), critical thinking, and Agile/Git workflows to ensure high-quality, scalable test automation
## Preferred Qualifications
• Experience testing AI/ML-powered web applications , including LLM-based features, chatbots, or AI agent workflows.
• Hands-on experience with performance/load testing (k6, JMeter) and AI/LLM performance metrics (TTFT, inter-token latency, token throughput).
• Experience in AI Ops / MLOps , or building/fine-tuning custom LLMs.
• Experience with observability and reporting tools such as Splunk , Grafana, Prometheus,

## Position Summary
We are seeking a senior, hands-on Performance Engineering Sr. QA Manager (M3) to lead a Performance Engineering Center of Excellence and own QA delivery for a product portfolio supporting high-transaction healthcare platforms. This role is ideal for a technical leader who can improve the reliability, scalability, and performance of EMR/EHR systems while mentoring strong QA teams and influencing engineering decisions with data. The candidate will shape performance strategy, build realistic workload models, diagnose complex bottlenecks, leverage observability, guide tooling architecture, and strengthen QA processes, quality metrics, and release readiness across systems built on microservices, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and modern frontend architectures.
## Key Responsibilities
• Lead the Performance Engineering CoE by defining performance standards, reusable frameworks, tooling strategy, governance practices, and enablement models that scale across product lines.
• Design realistic workload models, performance baselines, SLAs, and regression thresholds using production metrics, usage analytics, clinical transaction patterns, concurrency targets, throughput goals, and data volumes.
• Plan and execute load, stress, spike, soak, capacity, and scalability testing for high-volume workflows, then translate results into clear engineering recommendations and remediation priorities.
• Partner with development, architecture, DevOps, and database teams to identify and resolve bottlenecks across APIs, JVM, databases, caching, frontend, network, infrastructure, and cloud layers.
• Define automation coverage targets, guide scalable frameworks using Selenium, Playwright, RestAssured, or equivalent tools, and use coverage thresholds as part of release quality gates.
• Establish and track quality metrics across performance, scalability, reliability, security, accessibility, environment stability, release confidence, defect escape rate, and other non-functional requirements.
• Lead release readiness and QA governance reviews with clear entry and exit criteria, test strategy alignment, go/no-go recommendations, defect triage discipline, test evidence, release process adherence, and transparent risk communication.
• Improve QA productivity by reducing test cycle time, increasing defect detection efficiency, improving MTTR, strengthening sprint predictability, stabilizing environments, and reducing flaky automation.
• Partner with product, engineering, architecture, DevOps, and QA leaders during planning, design reviews, defect triage, release readiness, and product discussions to surface risks early and influence decisions with data.
• Support the Testing CoE by sharing reusable frameworks, standards, automation assets, lessons learned, and best practices that raise quality maturity across the organization.
## Required Qualifications and Skills
• 12+ years of progressive Quality Engineering and/or Performance Engineering experience, including 4+ years in formal people management or engineering leadership roles managing QA teams of five or more engineers.
• Ability to personally design, script, execute, analyze, and communicate performance tests and findings without relying solely on team execution.
• Hands-on experience with JMeter, LoadRunner, k6, Gatling, NeoLoad, or equivalent tools, including advanced scripting, protocol-level testing, workload modeling, distributed load generation, correlation, and parameterization.
• Ability to program and script in Java, Groovy, Python, or equivalent languages to build test scripts, utilities, custom extensions, and automation support.
• Strong working knowledge of modern distributed architectures, including microservices, APIs, API gateways, event-driven systems, containers, Java Spring Boot services, and React-based frontend or micro-frontend applications.
• Experience integrating quality and performance validation into CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or equivalent platforms, with automated execution, pipeline reporting, performance gates, and release thresholds.
• Strong understanding of system performance tuning across JVM internals, garbage collection, thread analysis, connection pools, application server configuration, OS and infrastructure utilization, and autoscaling behavior.
• Practical experience with Dynatrace or comparable APM tools, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, proactive monitoring, and performance analysis across Oracle, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, query tuning, and indexing.
• Strong troubleshooting capability across application code, JVM, database, network, infrastructure, and frontend layers, with the ability to translate findings into actionable engineering recommendations.
• Ability to define and guide automation strategy using Selenium, Playwright, RestAssured, API automation, regression coverage targets, framework governance, coverage thresholds, and automation ratio tracking.
• Hands-on experience using AI-assisted QA, test automation, code generation, analysis, or productivity tools to improve test coverage, delivery speed, engineering effectiveness, and quality outcomes.
• Proven ability to lead QA strategy, test planning, QA process maturity, automation maturity, release sign-off, quality metrics, NFR governance, process improvement, and stakeholder communication across product portfolios.
## Preferred Qualifications
• Healthcare technology, EMR, EHR, clinical workflow, patient-facing platform, or other mission-critical healthcare product experience.
• Experience building or scaling a Performance Engineering CoE, community of practice, shared tooling library, governance model, or internal enablement program.
• Experience with Kubernetes, container resource tuning, autoscaling, and modern cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
• Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7 and FHIR, along with awareness of healthcare data sensitivity, HIPAA, audit readiness, and collaboration with compliance, security, and legal partners.
## Working Conditions
• Regular collaboration with distributed engineering, QA, and DevOps teams across US and India time zones; the ability to communicate effectively across geographies and lead virtual teams is essential to success in this role.

McDermott, Will & Schulte LLP is building one of the most ambitious AI programs in the legal industry — and quality is not an afterthought. The AI Solutions QA Analyst must have experience using AI tools (eg. Claude, ChatGPT or other) for the testing lifecycle. AI QA Analyst partners directly with our AI Solutions Analysts and engineering team to ensure every solution we ship is tested, reliable, and production-ready — leveraging AI itself to do it faster and more thoroughly than traditional QA ever could.

Shape quality standards for an entirely new category of legal AI solutions — from the ground up
Work with frontier AI tools to build and run tests faster than traditional QA methods allow
High-visibility role reporting to Director of QA with direct impact on every solution the team ships
Remote-first, technically rigorous team that takes production quality seriously

Own the full QA lifecycle for AI-powered solutions — from unit and integration testing through system, performance, and scalability testing

Champion a quality culture across the delivery team — making testing a natural part of the development workflow, not a gate at the end

AI fluency — you use AI tools actively and can direct leading AI platforms to generate, evaluate, and refine test cases
4+ years of formal QA experience, including writing and executing test scripts across the full testing lifecycle
Strong experience with unit, integration, system, and regression testing — both manual and automated
Hands-on experience integrating test suites into CI/CD pipelines; Azure DevOps experience strongly preferred
Demonstrated ability to design boundary and edge case tests for complex, data-driven applications
Understanding of performance and scalability testing concepts; experience with load testing tools a plus
Solid grasp of defect tracking, test documentation, and quality metrics reporting
Strong analytical thinking — you approach untested AI behavior the way an engineer approaches an unknown system
BS in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent experience
Preferred:
Experience testing AI-powered applications — prompt-driven systems, agentic workflows, or LLM-integrated tools
Familiarity with AI-assisted test generation workflows and code-generating platforms
Exposure to security testing principles in collaboration with a dedicated security team
Experience in legal, financial services, or other regulated industry environments

## Job Description:
## About PrestoSports
PrestoSports, a Jonas Software company, builds the technology behind college athletics. Our website platform powers more than 1,500 athletic conference and college websites, and our PrestoStats platform is used by sports information directors across the NCAA, NAIA, NJCAA and other governing bodies to score games and publish results live.
We are a product and engineering team that has gone all in on AI-assisted development. Our in-house AI delivery platform turns well-defined plans into tested, reviewed software far faster than a traditional process, which means great product thinking is now the biggest driver of what we can ship. The annual salary range for this role is between $90,000 - $100,000 USD.
## About the role
We are looking for a Product Owner to own our CMS product line: the platform that runs the athletic websites fans, recruits, media and administrators visit every game day. You will be the product expert and the voice of the customer for CMS, deciding what gets built and why, and making sure every release lands well with schools, conferences and our own teams.
You will join at an important moment. We are in the middle of redesigning the CMS admin experience, the tools athletic communications staff use every day to publish schedules, rosters, stories and results. You will help shape and deliver that redesign, along with the longer-term move to our next-generation CMS platform.
You will work closely with our developers, a peer Product Owner for our Stats products, and our marketing, sales, support and implementation teams, reporting to the VP of Product and Development.
## What you will do
• Own the roadmap. Maintain the CMS product roadmap, keep it current as priorities and customer needs change, and adjust it each quarter with the VP of Product and Development.
• Plan and write the work. Use our AI delivery platform every day to turn customer needs and strategy into clear plans, user stories and testable acceptance criteria in Jira.
• Continue the CMS admin redesign. Define the requirements, gather feedback from athletic communications staff, and guide the redesign from plan to release.
• Review and accept what ships. Our developers review the code; you review the product. Test new features hands-on in preview environments, check them against acceptance criteria, and accept them or send them back with clear feedback.
• Triage support escalations. Vet bug reports and requests from our support team, add what developers need to act on them, set priority and route them to the right developer.
• Equip go-to-market teams. Give the first review on release positioning and launch material, brief support before every release, and give marketing the story behind bigger releases.
• Be the CMS expert. Know the platform better than anyone, talk with customers regularly, and use data from support, sales and site analytics to back your decisions.
## Products you will own
• CMS platform: current CMS and the next-generation platform, the admin redesign, migration and feature parity
• Front end and site design: templates, components, accessibility and performance across 1,500+ sites
• PrestoAI: AI-generated game recaps and athlete bios inside the CMS
• Camps and Forms: registration and forms tools for athletic departments
• Sidekick and Shots: roadmap, releases and customer feedback
• Custom development: scoping and acceptance of custom work for conferences and schools
## What we are looking for
Required
• 3+ years as a Product Owner, Product Manager or Business Analyst on a SaaS or web platform, ideally a multi-tenant CMS.
• A track record of writing clear user stories and testable acceptance criteria, and owning a backlog end to end in Jira.
• Hands-on use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) in daily work, and the judgment to review AI output critically.
• Working technical fluency: how websites are built and hosted, HTML and CSS basics, APIs and data formats, and how code moves from development to production.
• Strong writing. Plans, tickets, release notes and help articles are at the core of this job.
• Comfortable working directly with customers and internal teams, and able to say no and explain why.
Nice to have
• Experience in college athletics, especially athletic communications or sports information.
• Experience redesigning an admin or content-management interface, or leading a platform migration.
• Familiarity with web accessibility (WCAG), SEO and site performance.
• Experience with Salesforce and Google Analytics.
• Exposure to AI-assisted or agentic development workflows.
